column36: Determiner la qualite de la polypharmacie chez les aines : une approche basee sur l'intelligence artificielle
column37: La prise de plusieurs medicaments, la polypharmacie, est de plus en plus commune, surtout chez les personnes agees. Pour l'instant, il n'est pas possible de bien departager quelles polypharmacies apportent des benefices et quelles sont nefastes. En effet, le nombre de combinaisons de medicaments possibles est imposant, et prendre en compte les caracteristiques individuelles de chacune des personnes rend la situation tres complexe. L'intelligence artificielle permettra de comprendre ces elements pour en degager des normes. Dans ce projet, j'utiliserai le Systeme integre de surveillance des maladies chroniques du Quebec, qui contient les informations sur les reclamations de medicaments depuis 1996 pour l'ensemble des aines du Quebec atteints de maladies chroniques, de meme que leurs informations sur les services medicaux, les hospitalisations et le deces. Ces donnees, decrivant l'exposition aux medicaments de chaque individu, permettront d'entrainer un systeme expert base sur l'intelligence artificielle pour etablir quelles combinaisons, sequences, durees de traitement sont associes a des effets nefastes (ex. hospitalisations, deces) en tenant compte des conditions medicales et sociodemographiques de la personne. Les resultats serviront a developper la surveillance de la polypharmacie dans la population et apportera des connaissances nouvelles sur l'usage de medicaments qui pourraient changer la pratique clinique. L'utilisation de l'intelligence artificielle pour decouvrir des patrons d'utilisation de medicaments en lien avec les evenements de sante peut neanmoins poser des enjeux ethiques et sociaux, par exemple si les resultats sont susceptibles d'accroitre des inegalites entre differents sous-groupes de la population. Avec l'appui de plusieurs experts et chercheurs, j'evaluerai ces elements afin que les resultats obtenus soient acceptables socialement et conformes aux normes ethiques et legales.

column36: Monitoring and evaluation of Canada's Healthy Eating Strategy
column37: Poor dietary intake is a leading risk factor for non-communicable disease in Canada. Pre-packaged foods high in sodium, sugars and saturated fats account for an increasing proportion of the food supply, making it increasingly challenging for Canadians to make healthy choices. This program of work aims to evaluate Canada's Healthy Eating Strategy through a collaboration between the Office of Nutrition Policy and Promotion at Health Canada and the University of Waterloo. The Healthy Eating Strategy was announced in 2016 as a landmark policy framework to address dietary risk factors for chronic disease, and incorporates a variety of policy approaches, including updates to Canada's Food Guide and restrictions on food and beverage marketing to children. Health Canada is now in the process of developing approaches to: (1) monitor the extent and impacts of food and beverage marketing to children in Canada, (2) evaluate the short-term impacts of Canada's new Food Guide, and (3) evaluate the Healthy Eating Strategy as a whole. This program of work will utilize the research expertise of the Health Systems Impact Fellow to address these three needs. The objectives of this work will be supported by data from the International Food Policy Study (IFPS) at the University of Waterloo, which collects annual data on key food policy indicators from adults and youth across six countries, including Canada. Data from the IFPS will provide information that is critical to the evaluation of the Healthy Eating Strategy, such as frequency and sources of exposure to food and beverage marketing. The Fellow will lead data analysis and knowledge translation activities for the three objectives described above, and will serve as a liaison between Health Canada and the University of Waterloo to ensure efficient and appropriate use of the data. Ultimately, this work will help to ensure the Healthy Eating Strategy has a positive impact on the health and quality of life of Canadians.

column36: Guidelines for Evaluating Service Programming for Autistic Adults: A Patient-Oriented Perspective on Service Evaluation using Functional Criteria
column37: Currently there are few standards for evaluating service delivery, and since health care service delivery is a domain of the provinces, new health care services need to be tested and evaluated in each province before being widely offered. This leads to inefficiency in evaluations as well as unequal access to new services across the country. Also, the evaluations that are done are usually based on what the service delivery organization values about the programming rather than what the patient community served by the programming values. This project proposes creating sets of guidelines for evaluating service programs for autistic adults using functional criteria, criteria based on functional needs rather than diagnosis, determined by stakeholder engagement, including engagement with autistic adults, clinicians, and service providers, via focus groups. These guidelines would account for the variability of symptoms that can present in autistic adults, due to the focus on functional needs rather than diagnosis, and these guidelines would also increase efficiency and comparability in service evaluation and health care service delivery to the autism community. These guidelines, being informed by the needs and wants of the autism community, provide an opportunity for autistic adults to have a say in how service delivery and evaluation is done and how service programs can be designed for them.

column36: Improving End of Life Care: Expanding the 3 Wishes Project Hospital-wide
column37: Dying is a universal part of life, but the dying process can cause suffering and distress for patients and families. Current end-of-life care often focuses on reducing shortness of breath and pain. However, more holistic care recognizes the patient as an individual, also helping with difficult social and psychological aspects of personhood. The 3 Wishes Project (3WP) provides compassionate individualized care that honours the life and dignity of dying patients by eliciting terminal wishes from patients and their families, then families and clinicians implement them. Examples include playing music, trips outside, pet visitation, and spiritual ceremonies. Most wishes are simple and cost little, but can be priceless. Research in the intensive care unit (ICU) where the 3WP began shows that implementing wishes humanizes the dying process for families, and makes practice more meaningful for clinicians. My goal is to develop a 3WP for patients dying on the medical wards at St. Joseph's Healthcare Hamilton. Patients dying on hospital wards may benefit from even more personalized care. When not dependent on technology, patients can directly share the wishes they find most comforting. Families can be more supportive with less decision-making. Clinicians on the ward tend to have longer relationships with patients, which could create a better team approach to palliative care. During this career award, I will conduct a survey to understand factors that may help or hinder the 3WP on the wards. With input from patients, families, and clinicians, I will develop a strategic implementation plan. To understand if the 3WP can be implemented and sustained on the wards, I will evaluate the number of patients enrolled, and through interviews I will explore the effect of the 3WP on family grief and clinician engagement. Developing and evaluating the 3WP outside of ICU will help ensure more individualized, holistic, compassionate end-of-life care for patients dying on hospital wards.

column36: Evaluation economique d'interventions qui touchent le logement et la sante : eclairer les decisions, reduire les inegalites sociales de sante et preparer l'avenir pour une societe resiliente post-pandemie.
column37: Les evaluations economiques en sante sont des outils qui permettent de prendre en consideration l'efficience economique d'interventions en sante, c'est-a-dire d'en comparer les couts et les benefices en fonction des objectifs vises. Dans le secteur public, l'efficience economique est un enjeu ayant un grand pouvoir d'influence sur les decisions, et cela est tout a fait comprehensible : il en va de l'interet public de s'assurer que les ressources collectives sont mobilisees de facon a produire les meilleurs resultats possibles. Le present programme de recherche place le logement sous la loupe des evaluations economiques en sante pour plusieurs raisons. D'abord, le logement est une responsabilite qui touche l'ensemble des paliers de gouvernements et qui concerne la totalite de la population : tout le monde a besoin d'un toit. Ensuite, l'exposition aux conditions de logement est importante et repetee, puisqu'il s'agit d'un lieu central du quotidien, particulierement dans le contexte actuel. La pandemie a d'ailleurs mis en lumiere les inegalites de logement et les consequences disproportionnees pour les groupes les plus vulnerables (personnes agees, groupes autochtones, victimes de violence, etc.). Les decisions quant aux investissements publics ayant pour effet de modifier l'offre de logement ont des impacts a grande portee sur la sante physique et mentale des populations. Les autorites canadiennes de sante publique ont identifie le logement comme un des quatre domaines d'intervention a fort potentiel d'impact pour favoriser la resilience et l'equite en sante post-pandemie. Comme son titre l'indique, ce stage postdoctoral vise a realiser une analyse des couts et benefices d'interventions qui touchent le logement et la sante, au Quebec, de facon a guider les decisions et reduire les inegalites sociales de sante. Les conclusions seront applicables a l'ensemble du Canada et seront utiles dans la transition peri/post-pandemie.

column36: Expanding national surveillance of food and nutrition in Canada: Development and knowledge translation of indicators for eating behaviour and food environments from healthy and sustainable food systems
column37: Understanding the foods and beverages that Canadians consume is important for preventing chronic disease and promoting health and well-being. Currently, data on consumption of foods and beverages and eating behaviour in Canada are collected at distant time points, almost 10 years apart. This data provides a limited snapshot for government to make decisions about nutrition policy and programming. One of the Public Health Agency of Canada's main activities is to monitor and report on the state of health and health behaviours among Canadians. Currently, the Agency provides information on the amount of fruits and vegetables and sugar-sweetened beverages consumed. The Agency has an opportunity to update these measures to include monitoring of a range of food and nutrition behaviours, for example, using nutrition labelling to help make food purchases. Further, current research suggests that behaviours are affected by physical and social environments (food environment) and policies that influence the sustainability of the food supply (food system). However, a comprehensive framework of measures that includes food environments and food systems currently does not exist for Canada. The proposed work will identify existing questionnaires and assessments used at global, federal, provincial, and territorial levels to measure food and nutrition behaviour, food environments, and food systems. We will search current literature and work with partners across Canada to develop a framework for food and nutrition measures that will be integrated into the Agency's national surveillance strategy. We will also survey a range of audiences and collaborators from government, non-profit organizations, policymakers, and researchers to develop a strategy for communicating the framework. The proposed work will improve the health of Canadians and the health system by providing ongoing monitoring of food and nutrition in Canada to inform policy and programming decisions.

column36: Canadian Network on Hepatitis C (CanHepC): From Discovery to Implementation
column37: Hepatitis C is a liver disease caused by infection with the hepatitis C virus (HCV) and affecting 71 million people worldwide. In Canada, an estimated 250,000 people are living with HCV yet over 40% are unaware of their infection. HCV is a major cause of chronic liver disease including liver cancer and is responsible for more years of life lost than any other infection. The development and broad availability of direct acting antivirals (DAAs) that can cure HCV in >95% of treated individuals has been a major game changer. Together with proven ways to prevent infections, testing and diagnosis, DAAs present a unique opportunity to eliminate the virus. This has triggered a global push to eliminate HCV led by the World Health Organization and endorsed by Canada in 2016 with the goal of 80% reduction in chronic HCV infections by 2030. Despite this commitment, transmission of HCV in Canada continues to rise at an alarming rate. The major challenge in HCV elimination is that it disproportionately affects priority populations with limited access to healthcare including people who inject drugs, Indigenous peoples, people with experience in the prison system, newcomers to Canada, and gay and bisexual men who have sex with men. The Canadian Network on Hepatitis C (CanHepC) was established in 2015 as the first National Collaborative Research Network dedicated to HCV research. CanHepC combines a collaborative training and research program, bringing together over 100 members across Canada including researchers, trainees, and knowledge-users. In the next funding cycle, our infrastructure will be expanded to support research with direct impact on priority populations to prevent new HCV infections, reach the undiagnosed and engage them into care, treatment and assessing the long-term health implications of HCV infection. We expect to generate new knowledge and priority population specific tools and approaches to accelerate Canada's progress towards HCV 2030 elimination targets.

column36: The Effect of Gut Microbiota Metabolites on Histone Acetylation and Gene Expression in Normal Muscle and During Rhabdomyolysis
column37: The colony of micro-organisms populating the intestines, known as the gut microbiota, greatly affects human health and function. Specifically, it regulates distant organs by producing metabolites, which are released into circulation. In muscle, these metabolites are known to influence both composition and function. For example, a specific bacterium has been shown to enhance endurance, through the production of muscle-affecting metabolites. However, the exact way in which these metabolites affect muscle is still unclear. Basing ourselves on work previously done in different organs, we believe that they exert a direct influence over the muscle's genetic machinery, resulting in changes in gene expression. In turn, these gene expression modifications would affect the composition and function of muscle. In fact, through this mechanism, we believe that gut microbiota metabolites could contribute to preventing or resolving certain forms of muscular damage. Therefore, the aim of this project will be to determine whether gut microbiota metabolites affect genetic machinery, causing gene expression changes in muscle, and whether these changes can prevent or resolve muscular damage caused by a genetic disease. To do so, we will develop both 2D and 3D cellular models of healthy and damaged muscle, which we will subject to the appropriate metabolites. Biochemical techniques will be used to infer potential changes at specific steps along the gene expression pathway and to determine whether muscle damage has been alleviated at the cellular level. This project will be crucial in determining the specific molecular pathway linking the gut microbiota and muscle, offering a promising target for the development of future therapies for muscle injury, disease or performance.

column37: Definie comme une douleur qui persiste au-dela de 3 mois, la douleur chronique (DC) touche 1 adulte sur 5 (23 % des femmes et 16 % des hommes). Malgre des decennies de recherche sur la DC et son traitement, on constate malheureusement que la prise en charge de cette condition continue d' etre sous-optimale. On reconnait cependant que l'approche a privilegier doit etre multidisciplinaire. L'utilisation d'une approche multidisciplinaire est cependant parsemee de defis et les approches physiques et psychologiques sont souvent sous-utilisees (vs les medicaments). Bien que de nombreuses etudes aient identifie le sexe biologique comme un predicteur de l'utilisation des traitements contre la douleur, l'association entre l'utilisation des approches physiques/psychologiques et le genre est moins claire. Ainsi, mon projet de recherche aura pour objectif de mesurer les associations entre le sexe, le genre et l'usage d'approches physiques/ psychologiques dans le traitement de la DC. Pour repondre a ces objectifs, une banque de donnees existante issue du recrutement de 1935 personnes vivant avec de la DC (Cohorte COPE) sera utilisee. Associe a differents aspects entourant les maladies, le genre constitue une variable importante a mesurer afin de mieux comprendre les inegalites de sante, l'evolution des maladies et les effets des traitements. Ainsi ce projet permet de promouvoir une science plus rigoureuse et egalitaire et d'elargir notre comprehension des determinants sociaux de la sante.

column36: Exploring Repeated Clinical Encounters: A Participatory, Arts-informed Project for Women and Gender Minorities Living with Chronic Illness
column37: This research investigates frequent and prolonged healthcare interactions as a potential illness-induced stressor faced by women and gender minorities (WGM) living with chronic illnesses (CI). Autoethnographic research from feminist disability studies and medical sociology detail the ongoing distress of living CI and navigating healthcare, especially as experienced by WGM. While considerable research establishes a correlation between chronic stress, Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, and the subsequent development of CI, little information exists on effects of ongoing healthcare interactions. The importance of this research is threefold: 1) auto-immune disease in women is on the rise, 2) WGM face systemic barriers in care and 3) stress-related illness is overrepresented in gender minorities. The primary research question of this study is: how are women and gender minorities living with chronic illness affected by continually navigating healthcare interactions? This research aims to 1) generate new knowledge regarding experiences of medical micro-trauma and acknowledge promising practices as reported by participants; 2) use art-based resources to promote collaborative care between people with CI and their healthcare practitioners; and 3) develop patient-informed practice recommendations for healthcare practitioners. To achieve its aims, this research will involve the recruitment of 12 participants for arts-based workshops where they will reflect on their illness experiences, and a subsequent focus group to develop the practice recommendations. To foreground patient experience, this research employs a feminist intersectional lens and gender-based analysis. Finally, the outcomes of this research will be compiled in a zine to distribute to stakeholders in Canadian healthcare.

column36: The APIIC Study: Adapting a Preventive Intervention to the Indigenous Context
column37: The APIIC study (Adapting a Preventive Intervention to the Indigenous Context) aims to extend the reach of the PreVenture program, a personality-targeted, brief preventive intervention for youth mental health, by adapting it for young Indigenous people in Canada. Historically, Indigenous voices have been absent from research on mental health. Indeed, there is a lack of data and validated measures for these communities as well as a neglect for their unique cultural context in mental health research and service development. There is a need for more collaborative engagement and efforts to ensure that services are informed by their lived experiences and self-identified needs and are culturally sensitive and appropriate, especially for young people. This study will therefore be undertaken in partnership with Indigenous communities. PreVenture has been tested in many countries and has proven efficacious to delay and reduce adolescent use of alcohol and cannabis as well as reduce symptoms of depression, anxiety and conduct disorders. Considering this evidence, we aim to culturally adapt the intervention in partnership with three Indigenous communities while maintaining the core evidence-based principles and approach of the program. We will collaborate with youth and other members of these communities to determine what their mental health needs are, and how they would like to collaborate with us to adapt this program. Throughout, we will collect information on the process of adapting an intervention together with Indigenous youth and other stakeholders in the community to provide records of how such collaborative partnerships may take place. Finally, we will implement the adapted intervention in the communities, and evaluate its efficacy.

column36: Evolution de l'adhesion aux mesures efficaces de prevention contre la COVID-19 par les jeunes du secondaire - l'influence des evenements scolaires lies a la pandemie
column37: Le projet cherche a verifier si depuis la premiere vague et sa periode de confinement, les pratiques preventives mises en place par les adolescents contre la COVID-19 ont varie en fonction de leur niveau d'exposition aux evenements scolaires lies a la pandemie. En mars dernier, les jeunes ont vu leur vie chamboulee en raison de la pandemie, ayant dû interrompre leurs etudes et terminer l'annee en mode virtuel. Ayant largement adhere aux mesures de prevention durant cette periode, ils ont depuis reintegre les ecoles, soulignant le besoin de suivre l'evolution de leur adhesion aux mesures preventives et ses determinants dans ce groupe qui pourrait devenir un des vecteurs importants de la maladie. Le projet fait partie de la plateforme de recherche COMPASS-Quebec lancee en 2016-17. Elle accueille une cohorte de plus de 4000 jeunes de la premiere a la quatrieme annee du secondaire qui ont repondu a un questionnaire en ligne s'enquerant de leur sante, de leurs connaissances, opinions et de leurs comportements en mai-juin 2020. Ce m eme questionnaire sera distribue electroniquement un an plus tard (printemps 2021) aux eleves des 29 ecoles participantes. Les donnees entourant les evenements scolaires lies a la pandemie (p. ex : passage de classes en mode virtuel) seront amassees durant cet intervalle en collaboration avec les etablissements scolaires avec lesquels les chercheurs ont etabli au cours des ans, a l'aide des directions de sante publique regionales, un partenariat a l'avantage des eleves. Les mesures preventives efficaces (p. ex : lavage des mains, port du masque) auront quant a elles ete evaluees aux deux points de mesures. Les resultats cette etude bonifieront notre comprehension des impacts de la pandemie sur les comportements des jeunes et sur ses determinants.

column36: Engineering MicroMod CAR T-Cells To Overcome the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment in Myeloma
column37: Multiple myeloma (MM) is a malignant disease of immune cells called plasma cells characterized by immune suppression, bone lesions, and kidney failure. MM accounts for 12% of all new blood cancer diagnoses in Canada, with over 3300 Canadians diagnosed per year. Recent treatment advancements have prolonged survival; however, essentially all patients suffer multiple relapses and succumb to disease progression. Chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy is a new approach that involves harnessing the patient's own immune cells, called T-cells, and re-engineering them to seek out and destroy tumour cells. While this immunotherapy approach has shown success in other blood cancers, CAR T-cell therapy has only produced mild responses in MM with a high incidence of relapse. Recent evidence points towards the MM tumour microenvironment (TME), the compartment where the MM cells are located, as a potential factor in CAR T-cell failure. The TME contains a mixed cell population that supports MM growth. In particular, MM cells have been shown to polarize certain immune cells towards a MM-supporting role. These cells have been shown to protect MM cells from chemotherapy and immunotherapy. Recent findings have found that engineering CAR T-cells to secrete pro-immune molecules such as IL-12, or to remove certain molecules such as IL-6 can modulate the TME. By engineering MicroMod CAR T-cells to secrete IL-12 and remove IL-6, I aim to create a more pro-immune TME to achieve more durable responses following CAR T-cell therapy in MM. The results from this study will inform future CAR T-cell studies and contribute towards developing new treatments for this population of patients that desperately needs new therapeutic options.

column36: Cognitive testing for early detection of Alzheimer's disease in people with Down syndrome: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
column37: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is an increasing problem for people with Down syndrome (DS) . AD is a neurodegenerative disease which is characterized by brain lesions, multiple cognitive symptoms such as memory loss accompanied by a gradual autonomy loss. The development of brain lesions can appear years before AD. Through this progressive neuronal loss, patients can firstly begin to have a a perception of cognitive difficulties, i.e., a subjective cognitive decline (SCD). This preclinical phase ends with the onset of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) which is characterized by a set of cognitive symptoms, including memory loss while not affecting the daily living activities functioning. Knowing that people with DS have already pre-existing cognitive deficits, screening at the preclinical and clinical stages of AD therefore cannot be done through traditional cognitive tests. To date, several cognitive tests have been developed to screen for cognitive changes related to the development of AD in people with DS. A recent study has shown that difficulties in executive functions and memory are early signs of AD and especially of the MCI stage in individuals with DS. Knowing that cognitive tests adapted to people with DS finely assess memory and executive functions, we believe that these tests would make it possible to diagnose as many people with DS as possible in one of the early stages of AD by detecting only those actually in one of these stages. The present research will first, through a systematic review, identify studies that have used cognitive tests for the diagnosis of AD, MCI or SCD in people with DS. Then, through a meta-analysis, the real magnitude of each of the tests will be quantified thus putting them on the same basis of analysis in order to compare them.

column36: Elucidating the Relationship between Maternal Depression and Externalizing Problem Behaviours in Offspring: A Mediator Analysis Examining Parenting Style, Heart Rate, and Sleep
column37: Exposure to maternal depression (MD) during childhood is linked to adverse developmental outcomes and an increased risk of psychopathology in offspring, including externalizing problem behaviours (EPB); however, the mechanisms underlying this relationship are not well understood. Harsh parenting style, resting heart rate abnormality, and poor childhood sleep have all been linked with MD, EPD, or both, suggesting that they may be involved in the transmission of psychopathology from mothers to children. Using data from an ongoing eHealth intervention trial involving mothers with depression and their 2-5 year old children, this study will examine (a) parenting style, (b) maternal and child HR, and (c) child sleep, as mediating factors in the relationship between MD and EPB in childhood. We will use a combination of questionnaire and Fitbit (i.e., photoplethysmography heart rate tracker) data to assess these variables. At post-intervention, these relationships will be re-examined, providing important information about how behavioural and/or physiological changes are linked to symptom remission in mothers and children. Results from the proposed project will provide a better understanding of the factors underlying the intergenerational transmission of psychopathology in early childhood. These findings will be crucial in the development of family-focused interventions to improve health and developmental outcomes for young children exposed to MD.

column36: Evaluating the population genetic structure of Canada for forensic human identity applications.
column37: A critical component for forensic cases involving biological samples is the generation of a deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) profile and its corresponding statistics, which estimate the rarity of a particular DNA profile within a given population. These statistics are calculated from allele frequency data generated from extensive population studies. Currently, such large-scale studies relevant to the field of forensics involving Canadian populations are scarce. Previous literature mainly provides allele frequency data for Canadian Indigenous populations and individuals of European descent, which may be non-reproducible when investigating other populations within Canada. Another issue with currently established testing methods is that they provide only a superficial way of comparing allele data using DNA length. Using a newer method of DNA analysis known as massively parallel sequencing (MPS), higher resolution allele data can be produced, allowing for a more thorough generation of accurate DNA profiles. Furthermore, MPS can generate additional ancestry and phenotype data, which can be utilized as critical information for investigative purposes such as in missing persons cases or disaster victim identification. The objective of this research is to generate allele frequencies, ancestry, and phenotype data using MPS for European, East Asian, Oceanic, American, African, South Asian, and Southwest Asian Canadian populations. The generation of novel population statistics from this research will have a significant impact for forensic cases as it increases the ability to better estimate the rarity of a DNA profile within any major population in Canada. Additionally, data generated in this project will explore the unique genetic diversity and make-up of Canada's populations.

column36: Characterization of Pressure-induced Changes in The Human Eye with Novel Organotypic Approach
column37: Glaucoma, a sight-threatening disease with no curative treatment, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGC) and their axons in the optic nerve. Elevated intraocular pressure (IOP), a prominent risk factor of glaucoma, causes pathological changes in the retina and optic nerve supportive tissue called the lamina cribosa (LC) in experimental models. However, the initial effects of elevated IOP in intact human eyes remain unclear due to a lack of appropriate models. I propose to study the early changes in the human eye following pressure insult with a novel organotypic approach. Specifically, donated eyes are attached to artificial anterior segments, which ensure the preservation of retinal health and accurate manipulation of IOP with perfusion of aqueous humor. Using this model, eyes will be perfused to maintain normal (21 mmHg) IOP for the control group or elevated but physiologically relevant (60mmHg) IOP for the treatment group. My first aim is to assess the morphological changes in the eyes following elevated IOP. Perfused eyes will be imaged with ocular coherence tomography to examine glaucomatous changes in the retina. The retina and LC will be further examined with immunohistochemistry and confocal microscopy, in which biomarkers will be quantified to evaluate tissue health. My second aim is to assess the functional changes in the eyes following elevated IOP. The retina and LC will be by analyzed by single-cell sequencing to characterize cell-types-specific transcriptomic differences, which will then be verified by qPCR. Data from this project will elucidate the role of elevated IOP in the pathogenesis of glaucoma in human eyes, potentially aiding the discovery of novel therapeutic targets.

column36: Role d'IGFBP2 dans le developpement de la nephropathie dans le diabete de type 2 et de la fibrose tubulaire
column37: La nephropathie diabetique (ND) est une complication renale affectant plusieurs patients diabetiques et c'est l'une des premieres causes d'insuffisance renale menant a la dialyse ou une transplantation. Mon etude porte sur la fibrose renale, qui est un phenomene irreversible dans la maladie renale chronique. Les cellules tubulaires sont les principales cellules qui produisent la fibrose. Leur dysfonction est un evenement tardif a la ND. Plusieurs facteurs sont importants pour la fonction des cellules tubulaires. Un de ses facteurs est l'Insulin-like growth factor, molecule qui est egalement controlee par les IGF Binding Proteins (IGFBP). Or, notre equipe a decouvert que les niveaux de IGFBP2 etaient diminues chez les jeunes patients diabetiques de types 2 qui avaient une fonction renale alteree. L'objectif de ce projet est donc d'etudier le role de l'IGFBP2 dans le developpement de la fibrose tubulaire dans un modele de souris diabetiques de type 2. Nos resultats preliminaires confirment que les cellules tubulaires isolees de souris diabetiques montrent des niveaux plus faibles d'IGFBP2 comparativement aux souris non-diabetiques. Notre hypothese est que le retablissement des niveaux d'IGFBP2 aura un effet positif sur les actions des Insulin-like growth factor, responsable d'une production de fibrose non controlee. Pour ce faire, nous utiliserons des souris qui surexpriment IGFBP2 et ainsi mesurer la presence de fibrose, de marqueurs de fibrose et la fonction renale.

column36: Implantation et impact d'un appareil portatif de monitorage pour augmenter la motivation a pratiquer l'activite physique chez les diabetiques de type 2 en soins de premiere ligne
column37: Le diabete de type 2 est une maladie qui touche de plus en plus de gens et qui peut affecter la qualite de vie. Il est reconnu que l'adoption de saines habitudes de vie permet de reduire le risque d' etre atteint de diabete et de diminuer les complications. Aujourd'hui, la technologie est en plein developpement. Des appareils portatifs permettant de mesurer le nombre de pas, la distance parcourue, les calories brûlees et la frequence cardiaque sont maintenant disponibles sur le marche. Encore peu d'etudes sont faites a leur sujet, notamment chez les patients atteints de maladies chroniques. Ainsi, les deux objectifs de l'etude sont de determiner l'impact du port d'une montre Fitbit sur la sante et la motivation a pratiquer l'activite physique chez les personnes atteintes de diabete de type 2 ainsi que de determiner la faisabilite d'utiliser cette montre en soins de premiere ligne. Il s'agit etude de 3 mois realisee aupres de patients diabetiques suivis au GMF-U Quatre-Bourgeois. Les participants sont assignes au hasard a 1) groupe temoin, qui comprend une activite de promotion de l'activite physique faite par un kinesiologue ou 2) groupe intervention, où les participants portent en plus une montre Fitbit durant l'etude. Chaque participant assiste a 3 rencontres. Au debut et a la fin, un bilan de sante est fait et l'activite physique et la motivation sont mesurees a l'aide de deux questionnaires. a la toute fin, les participants du groupe intervention remplissent un questionnaire sur leur satisfaction et appreciation de la montre Fitbit. Si les resultats sont encourageants, des appareils comme des montres mesurant l'activite physique pourraient etre recommandes par les professionnels de sante a leurs patients pour les motiver a ameliorer leurs habitudes de vie.

column36: Metabolic modelling for drug development in Neisseria gonorrhoeae
column37: Neisseria gonorrhoeae is the bacteria that causes the sexually transmitted infection gonorrhea. Antimicrobial resistant (AMR) N. gonorrhoeae strains have become more common, leading to concerns about the rise of untreatable gonorrhea infections. There is, therefore, an urgent need for the development of new therapies to treat gonococcal infections. This project seeks to identify and characterize new targets for drug development by combing powerful computational models with state-of-the-art laboratory techniques. First, a computational model of N. gonorrhoeae metabolism will be developed using publicly available sequence data from over 7400 global gonococcal isolates. Representative strains will be grown in a variety of infection-mimicking culture conditions, and their growth characteristics will be used to validate and improve our computational model. The model will then be used to identify essential pathways through large scale simulations determining the impacts of single and tandem gene deletions on growth and viability. Pathways that appear to be essential for N. gonorrhoeae based upon my modeling will be validated by testing small molecule inhibitor and/or isogenic mutant strains during in vitro growth and human cell line-based infection conditions. Special emphasis will be placed on pairs of genes that, when inhibited together, confer a lethal phenotype as these pairs represent ideal targets for drug development. Key essential targets will then be tested in a 'humanized' mouse model established to be susceptible to gonorrheal infection. This approach will identify targets for future efforts in drug development, while also developing a well characterized metabolic model of N. gonorrhoeae for further research efforts.

column36: Sex differences in the brain
column37: The use of hormone therapy (HT) in aging women has been revolutionary in the prevention of cognitive decline that can emerge around the time of menopause. Although there are studies indicating HT can increase the risk of breast cancer, the absolute risk must be weighed against the benefits of treatment. There are different types of HT available, commonly including estrogens such as estradiol or estrone. Interestingly, the effect of HT varies with reproductive experience as estrone-based HT in nulliparous (never pregnant) rats enhances cognition and plasticity compared to deleterious effects seen in primparous (1 litter) rats. Since parity influences the efficacy of hormone treatment, it would be ideal to investigate the mechanism behind this phenomena in order to provide the most appropriate form of HT to women. As parity is associated with increased neuroinflammation in both women and mice, it is suspected this inflammation could be at the root of these differential effects of HT on cognition and plasticity with parity. We hypothesize that parity interacts with different estrogens to induce long-lasting effects on neuroplasticity and cognition, which is primarily mediated through neuroinflammation. The experiment will be conducted in female rats in order to determine the effect of estrone-based HT (Premarin) and estradiol-based HT (Progynova) in rats with varying reproductive history. Behavioural tests will be conducted measure the impact of the various HTs on spatial learning and memory. If certain forms of HT prove to be more effective than others in primparous or multiparous rats compared to nulliparous rats, this work would have implications for more personalized treatment of aging women that are receiving HT based on their reproductive experience.

column36: Reprogrammation metabolique en cancer : Role des enzymes UGT
column37: La perturbation de la voie de glucuronidation, mediee par enzymes UDP-glucuronosyltranferases (UGT), est associee au developpement et a la progression de multiples cancers. Cette voie metabolique pourrait participer a la reprogrammation metabolique, une caracteristique cle de la transformation et de la progression tumorale. Mon projet vise a etablir les perturbations associees a la forte expression de la voie UGT en leucemie lymphoide chronique (LLC) dans les modeles cellulaires et chez les patients. La LLC est la leucemie la plus frequence chez l'adulte, pour laquelle la voie UGT est associee a un pronostic defavorable et a la resistance au traitement. Les changements metaboliques pourraient s'etendre a des perturbations de nombreux metabolites au-dela des substrats de l'UGT, puisque ces proteines forment un reseau complexe d'interactions avec d'autres enzymes du metabolisme cellulaire influencant potentiellement leurs fonctions et les metabolites associes. L'etendue des changements de concentrations de metabolites cellulaires sera evaluee en utilisant une combinaison d'approches metabolomiques ciblee et non ciblee. J'evaluerai si ces changements sont provoques par la fonction enzymatique de l'UGT, en incluant un modele surexprimant l'enzyme inactive. Une fois les voies metaboliques les plus perturbees identifiees, j'evaluerai leurs impacts sur le phenotype oncogenique. Ces travaux permettront d'identifier les voies metaboliques associees a ce marqueur de mauvais pronostique et a la resistance en cancer, ainsi que leurs effets oncogeniques. Ils pourraient aussi permettre d'identifier de nouvelles cibles therapeutiques pour les patients a haut risque exprimant fortement l'UGT.

column36: The Effects of the Gut Microbiota on Intestinal Epithelial Regeneration and Immune Tolerance
column37: Crohn's disease (CD) is form of inflammatory bowel disease that affects over 130,000 Canadians, with increasing prevalence especially in children. While genetic risk influences CD development, environmental factors such as the host intestinal microbiota, and its associated interactions with the immune system, are also implicated in development of CD. Recently however, resident commensals in the small intestine (e.g. Akkermansia muciniphila) were shown to promote an anti-inflammatory environment and immune tolerance to the gut microbiota by triggering IL-10 secretion by intraepithelial T-cells. This process is thought to be orchestrated in part by microbiota-mediated MHC-II regulation on intestinal epithelial cells. The secreted IL-10 by small-intestinal T-cells in response to resident commensals also feeds back on the intestinal stem cell (ISC) pool to regulate barrier protection. Beyond homeostasis, the exact function of this emerging Microbe -> MHC-II -> IL-10 -> ISC axis remains poorly characterized. In this project I will examine the ways in which MHC-II-inducing bacteria such as A. muciniphila regulate epithelial integrity and immune tolerance. I hypothesize that host microbial sensors (aka pattern recognition molecules; PRMs) including Nod2 are critical for the cross-talk between commensal microbes and intestinal epithelial cells to initiate the IL-10-dependent axis that contributes to barrier protection. My proposed studies will reveal new avenue of immune therapy to aid tissue regeneration in patients with IBD.

column36: Role of Extracellular Granzyme B in Age-related Macular Degeneration in Mouse Models
column37: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is a complex disease in which aging, genetics and environment all play significant roles. AMD affects more than 6 million individuals worldwide and treatment is an expensive, multidimensional healthcare issue in Canada. Here, I am investigating a potential target, Granzyme B (GzmB), that is a serine protease that plays a role in chronic inflammation and abnormal degradation of extracellular proteins. However, its role within the eye has not been thoroughly investigated. Thus, using a mouse model for early stage AMD, which is characterized by a thickened Bruch's Membrane (BM), I will characterize the mechanism of action of GzmB as well as its role in contributing to the abnormalities associated with early AMD by using methods such as, western blotting, immunofluorescence, immunoassays and electron microscopy. I hypothesize that GzmB contributes to AMD through the cleavage of key extracellular proteins that result in changes to the blood-retina barrier and ultimately, increased inflammation and vascular permeability of the outer retina, the area most affected by pathological changes associated with AMD. Through targeting and inhibiting GzmB as proposed here, our premise is that it will suppress the changes in the BM that present as some of the earliest indication of AMD development. The studies proposed here will assess GzmB as a potential target for future development of a first-in-class anti-protease drug to 1) suppress ECM breakdown in early AMD and 2) reduce the angiogenic and proinflammatory drive in outer retina associated with wet AMD. Inhibitors for Gzmb are already in clinical trails for other disease applications, and it may be of interest to see the inhibitors application in the eye.

column36: The role of community health navigators in the creation and execution of tailored plans to support self-management of chronic conditions in patients: An evaluation of the ENCOMPASS program
column37: Managing chronic conditions such as diabetes and high blood pressure can be confusing and complex for patients. Approximately 1 in 3 Canadian adults are living with two or more chronic conditions. Overall, $170 billion is spent annually by the Canadian healthcare system on chronic conditions. As the number of chronic conditions increases, so does the complexity of patient care plans. When patients have difficulty adhering to care plans, the risk of health complications rises and further strains the health system. Multiple social factors such as financial constraints, transportation, or language barriers, may hinder a patient's ability to follow their recommended care plan. column37: Chronic cough lasting for more than 8 weeks affects approximately 10-12% of adults worldwide and is one of the most common reasons for referral to secondary care. Existing PRO instruments that assess cough symptom severity have neither been tested for validity or responsiveness, nor made widely available. column36: Treating Inflammatory Bowel Disease by Developing Small Molecule Inhibitors of a Novel Protein Target
column37: Canada has one of the highest rates of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) worldwide and this is expected to rise in the next decade. IBD is a burden on patients, healthcare and society. Despite recent advances in IBD therapies, many patients do not respond to current treatments. IBD is described as a chronic, recurrent inflammation of the gastrointestinal tract and although various genetic and environmental factors have been associated with this disease, the cause of IBD is still unknown. Numerous genes are identified as a risk factor for IBD, however, not all have been explored. One of these genetic risk factors is a gene that codes for an active, atypical dual specificity phosphatase (DUSP). DUSPs are enzymes that remove a phosphate group from a protein and many are poorly characterized. Unpublished work from our lab shows that mice lacking the gene that encodes for this DUSP are protected from developing IBD. Since this DUSP is an active enzyme, its activity can be inhibited, making it a promising therapeutic target for IBD. We hypothesize that this DUSP is critical in promoting IBD and that inhibiting the active site of the DUSP using selective and potent small molecule inhibitors may prevent and/or reduce IBD-induced pathologies. This hypothesis will be explored in two aims. The first aim is to optimize the assay conditions for identifying small molecule inhibitors. 74,000 diverse compounds will then be tested against the DUSP to test for their ability to inhibit this enzyme. In the second aim, the promising compounds will be modified until effective, lead compounds are developed. Based on the evidence that this DUSP plays a role in IBD, potent small molecule inhibitors targeting this protein will hopefully provide a promising novel treatment for IBD patients.

column36: Measuring ventilation in lungs using a novel inert fluorinated (19F) gas multiple breath wash-out MRI technique to quantify treatment response in preschoolers with cystic fibrosis
column37: Cystic fibrosis (CF) is an incurable genetic lung disease, so potential therapies must start early to slow disease progression. A treatment called CFTR modulator therapy is promising for CF and works best when started before symptoms are visible in children. Current lung function tests only identify CF in children after symptoms appear, showing a strong clinical need for new measures of lung function that are sensitive to early-stage CF. Studying the lungs by inhaling and exhaling a gas is useful because it shows interesting behaviour in the lungs. This technique, called multiple-breath washout (MBW), is a lung test used clinically to separate health from disease, but is not sensitive enough for early-stage CF. A newer, sensitive MBW technique using xenon gas MRI can also be performed, but the signal decays over time in the presence of oxygen, making it difficult to image for long times where useful clinical insight is thought to be. MBW MRI with a fluorinated gas is attractive because it can be mixed with oxygen without signal decay, letting patients breath it for a long time. This method was shown to distinguish health from disease in adults with CF but not in children or treatment response. I believe this technique is sensitive enough to detect the presence of disease before symptoms of CF are visible in children. I hope to develop it by comparing it to the existing xenon and current clinical techniques in healthy children and children with stable CF, then see if it can detect the effectiveness of CFTR modulator therapy. The ability of fluorinated gas MBW MRI to study early-stage CF is essential for the development of new treatments and the improved long-term health of children with lung disease (ex. We predict this investigation will identify new mechanisms that regulate glucagon production. column36: 'Living' systematic review on thoracic imaging for the diagnosis of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19)
column37: People that are suspected of having coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) need accurate diagnostic tests to determine whether they are infected, so they can receive treatment & self-isolate to prevent the spread of infection. column36: Elucidating regulators of the tumor necrosis factor receptor-interacting protein with fork head-associated domain (TIFA) immune signaling pathway
column37: Our immune system's ability to detect infectious microbes is essential to mounting an effective immune response. One protein involved in this process is tumor necrosis factor receptor-interacting protein with fork head-associated domain (TIFA). The TIFA-dependent immune cascade is activated in response to metabolites released by certain life-threatening bacteria, including Neisseria meningitidis. This complex acts as a scaffold to assemble downstream signaling proteins that trigger inflammation by interacting with other proteins. I will utilize a large-scale genetic screen with CRISPR activation technology, which allows me to force individual genes throughout the entire genome to be overexpressed in cells while measuring the activity of the TIFA pathway. If a gene is involved in regulation, I will see a deviation from regular activity levels and will identify the gene. Then, I can cross-reference these genes to other known immune response genes to determine how the TIFA pathway interconnects with other immune pathways. All together, my studies will provide new understanding to a previously unrecognized immune response pathway and reveal potential options to regulate its activity so as to control inflammation in a manner that improves the outcome of both infectious and non-infectious immunopathogenic diseases.

column36: The trade-off from exploration to exploitation: the underlying mechanisms of healthy and at-risk aging
column37: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurological disease that leads to deficits in memory and executive function. AD prevalence is climbing at alarming rates in Canada. Families, communities, and health care systems are strained economically and emotionally from the resources that are being devoted to AD care. Treatment for AD is lagging because of the poorly understood neural and cognitive mechanisms that underly the symptoms. Exploration-exploitation is an emergent model that may help uncover these mechanisms and thus help facilitate future clinical assessment and treatment research. Exploration-exploitation posits that as people age, they tend to trade novelty seeking problem solving (i.e., exploration) for a reliance on prior knowledge (i.e., exploitation). This cognitive shift, in theory, maps onto the brain changes that are known to occur during healthy and even pathological aging. However, this cognitive-neural mapping has never been explicitly studied. The current study will develop a decision-making/ problem solving paradigm to be implemented during a brain scan procedure. The procedure will be delivered to people of different ages, including older adults from the Montreal Cohort who are at a high risk for AD. If a stronger reliance on exploitative behaviour is seen among those at-risk for AD, then this could signal the presence of a novel behavioural biomarker that can predict a forecasting AD diagnosis. It is essential to uncover not only the cognitive and neuromechanisms of healthy aging, but also pathological aging in order to facilitate the clinical assessment of at-risk geriatric populations, which could potentially outline new early preventative interventions.

column36: Neuronatin and SERCA uncoupling - a novel target for obesity?
column37: 25% of the Canadian population is considered obese and it is becoming imperative that research find alternative ways to circumvent obesity and its associated negative effects. A promising strategy is through increasing energy expenditure to shift the balance towards burning more calories than those consumed. An encouraging avenue of increasing energy expenditure is via the sarco(endo)plasmic reticulum Ca2+ ATPase (SERCA) pump. SERCA is responsible for transporting 2 Ca2+ ions from the cytosol into the sarcoplasmic reticulum using energy from ATP and accounts for up to 50% of the basal metabolic rate in skeletal muscle. Reducing SERCA efficiency through lowering its optimal coupling ratio of 2 Ca2+ per ATP will cause more ATP to be hydrolyzed for the same task, similar to a fuel inefficient car requiring more gas per kilometers travelled. Sarcolipin (SLN) is a small protein capable of reducing this coupling ratio and SLN knockout (KO) mice show reductions in energy expenditure and are more susceptible to high fat diet (HFD). Neuronatin (NNAT) is a protein that I have recently shown to be present in skeletal muscle and shares sequence homology with SLN. Our lab has recently shown NNAT to uncouple SERCA in cell culture and I plan to extend this work in a novel muscle-specific NNAT knockdown mouse model. Mice will be fed either a chow or HFD and whole-body energy expenditure will be measured using the Promethion metabolic caging system. Further, glucose and insulin tolerance tests will be performed and the SERCA coupling ratio will be determined in soleus and extensor digitorum longus muscles. This will be the first time a protein akin to SLN will have been discovered and characterized as a SERCA uncoupler, thus providing a completely novel target for combatting obesity.

column36: Assessing the Clinical Utility of Proviral DNA-based Antiretroviral Drug Resistance Testing in Individuals Living with Human Immunodeficiency Virus Type 1
column37: Globally, Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) infects 38 million people, including over 68,000 Canadians. These individuals must take antiretroviral therapy (ART) that blocks HIV replication and thereby significantly improves quality and duration of life. However, ART can be compromised by the emergence of HIV drug resistance (HIVDR). HIV evolves rapidly in a host because its reverse transcriptase enzyme makes errors during replication. If ART is not taken regularly, HIV may continue to replicate and these errors can introduce mutations that make HIV resistant to antiretrovirals. Current treatment guidelines recommend performing HIVDR testing before initiating ART so physicians can choose an appropriate ART regimen. HIVDR testing can only be performed on RNA from a patient's blood that contains high levels of HIV. This presents challenges when making treatment decisions for treating patients with undetectable HIV levels, especially those with incomplete or unknown treatment history, as traditional HIVDR testing cannot be performed. However, HIV integrates into a host's genome as proviral DNA and the prior circulating HIV variants in a host are archived in the proviral DNA. Hence, proviral DNA could be used to test for HIVDR, but it is not fully understood if DNA-based drug resistance testing is as reliable as current RNA-based methods. Thus, this project will use two studies to assess the concordance of HIVDR testing performed on HIV DNA and RNA samples in persons on ART with undetectable viral load. The first study will examine rates of concordance at the population level. The second will examine HIVDR in proviral DNA in a small cohort of participants using next-generation sequencing to investigate the persistence of drug resistance mutations in proviral DNA over time.

column36: Role of hypoxia signaling in placental trophoblast differentiation
column37: Preeclampsia is a common and serious disease during pregnancy. It presents as high blood pressure and blood vessel damage in mothers that can progress to organ failure, stroke, and death of the mother and/or baby. There is no cure except delivering the baby early, which poses immediate and long-term health risks for the prematurely delivered infant. The root cause of preeclampsia is improper development of the placenta – the temporary organ supporting growth of the baby in the womb. Little is known about why the placenta develops abnormally in these pregnancies, which makes developing safe and effective treatments challenging. Our research aims to fill this gap in understanding. In preeclamptic placentas, a chronic low oxygen environment persists due to dysregulated blood flow to the placenta. Our preliminary data show that low oxygen inhibits placental stem cell differentiation and may thus contribute to the poor placental development and function characteristic of pregnancies with preeclampsia; however, why this happens is not yet understood. Since low oxygen activates a group of regulatory proteins in cells known as the hypoxia-inducible factor (HIF), it is suspected that HIF plays a role. Therefore, we hypothesize that HIF activation impairs placental stem cell differentiation under low oxygen by regulating gene expression. In this study, we will test whether blocking HIF signaling restores the capacity of placental stem cells to differentiate under low oxygen. Furthermore, we will identify genes regulated by HIF that control placental differentiation, which may aid in developing novel therapeutics for prevention and management of preeclampsia.

column37: L'allaitement maternel est important pour la sante des meres et de leurs nourrissons. Il contribue notamment au renforcement du systeme immunitaire de ces derniers. Alors que sevit au Canada une deuxieme vague de la pandemie mondiale de COVID-19, nous ignorons encore les repercussions de cette crise sur l'allaitement maternel. Suivant le modele theorique du sentiment d'auto-efficacite a allaiter (SAEA), le developpement de la confiance des meres en leur capacite a allaiter pourrait etre influence par le contexte relevant de cette crise et par la disponibilite des services d'education prenatale. Dans cette optique, il est primordial de connaitre l'influence des services d'education prenatale de groupe (ePG) et en ligne (ePL), ainsi que du contexte de la COVID-19 sur l'allaitement maternel. But : Mesurer l'influence des services d'ePG/d'ePL et du contexte de la COVID-19 sur differents indicateurs lies a l'allaitement aupres de futures et nouvelles meres d'un premier enfant. Methode : etude correlationnelle predictive realisee a partir de donnees issues d'une etude d'une cohorte composee de 863 femmes enceintes d'un premier enfant, dont certaines ont ete exposees au contexte quebecois de la COVID-19 en fin de grossesse et/ou dans les semaines suivant la naissance. Differents modeles d'analyses seront utilises pour estimer l'influence des services educatifs et du contexte de la COVID-19 sur l'intention d'allaiter, l'evolution du SAEA, l'initiation et la duree de l'allaitement. Retombees: Les resultats pourront guider les prises de decisions visant une meilleure integration des services educatifs et de soutien en matiere d'allaitement tout au long de la trajectoire perinatale, en contexte de pandemie, ici comme a l'international.

column36: Understanding Young Friends in an Online Sample of Minor Attracted Persons
column37: This proposed research aims to further examine the phenomenon of friendships with children (young friends) among minor-attracted persons (MAPs) and how these social interactions are associated with MAPs' emotional congruence with children, psychological distress, loneliness, suicidality, and risk of sexual offending against a child. I recently completed an Honours thesis which was the first to directly examine young friends among MAPs and results showed a non-trivial margin of MAPs indicate they have at least one young friend. Moreover, findings showed a significant positive correlation between MAPs with young friends and suicidality. In view of the fact that these social relationships appear to be problematic and are still not fully understood, this area warrants further attention. Recruitment will consist of posting a call for participants to complete an online anonymous survey on multiple online MAP community forums and Twitter. A sample size of 250 participants is anticipated. Measures will include those examining emotional congruence with children, psychological distress, suicide behaviours, loneliness, and questions regarding previous sexual offences against children. Anticipated statistical analysis will consist of, where applicable, comparisons via standardized mean difference (Cohen's d), correlations, and logistic regressions with a potential to examine mediation and moderation models. It is imperative that we gain a better understanding of how and why MAPs seek young friends and how these social interactions are associated with MAPs mental health and risk of sexually offending against a child. With this better understanding we can better inform treatment practices for MAPs and potentially further prevent sexual offending against children.

column36: Defining the role of tissue resident immune cells in promoting or inhibiting ischemia reperfusion injury (IRI) and poorer clinical outcomes in kidney transplantation.
column37: Ischemia reperfusion injury (IRI) refers to damage caused when blood supply returns to an organ after oxygen deprivation, which can lead to severe malfunction of the organ. Notably, patients who receive kidney transplants from deceased donors have higher rates of IRI, rejection and damage compared to patients that receive transplants from living donors. Recent studies have identified discrete immune populations, such as innate lymphoid cells (ILCs), that promote tissue repair and aid in reducing damage caused by IRI. While certain subsets of ILCs contribute to inflammatory immune responses, other subsets control inflammation and promote tissue repair. However, the role of ILCs within IRI and kidney transplantation is not known. This research will examine the contribution of ILCs and other tissue-resident immune populations in protecting kidneys from transplant rejection and IRI. We suspect that kidneys from deceased donors contain fewer protective ILCs than kidneys from living donors, which may contribute to higher risk of IRI and rejection. Using advanced computational platforms, we will perform in-depth analyses of ILCs and other immune cells in deceased donors and living donors pre- and post- transplantation. This will involve analyzing cellular interactions and functional characteristics to identify protective and harmful immune cells in transplanted kidneys. The ultimate goal of this research is to define harmful immune cells that can be targeted to lower the risk of IRI in deceased donor transplants or identify protective immune cells to harness in cell-based immune therapies for transplantation. This will lead to improved patient recovery, more successful transplants, and reduced kidney disease morbidity.

column36: Beta-caryophyllene - a novel adjunct treatment for bacterial cystitis
column37: Bacterial cystitis (BC), commonly known as urinary tract infection (UTI), are among the most common bacterial infections affecting 150 million people worldwide each year. BC occurs most commonly in otherwise health women when bacteria enters the bladder. Approximately 25% of women who experience BC will suffer a current UTI within 6 months of the initial episode. Antibiotics are currently the treatment of choice for UTIs. However, antibiotics fail to eliminate a recurrence and some antibiotics are infective due to the rise in multi-drug resistant pathogens. This unmet need of effective therapy calls for new treatment approaches to this disorder. The endocannabinoid system (ECS) has recently been studied for its therapeutic effects in inflammatory disorders. The effects of the ECS are primarily mediated by the cannabinoid receptors type 1 (CB1) and type 2 (CB2). Unlike CB1, activation of CB2 does not induce psycho-active effects. CB2 activation has been shown to reduce pain and inflammation, making it an interesting target for inflammation of the urinary bladder. Beta-caryophyllene (BCP) can be found in Cannabis sativa and other plants such as cloves. It has been shown to activation CB2 receptors and help eliminate pain and infection. The proposed study will look at the therapeutic effects of BCP in a mouse model of BC. Mice bladder's will be infected with Escherichia coli and left for 24 hours to develop BC. In order to study the efficacy of BCP in treating pain and infection, mice will be given either: saline, BCP or antibiotics. We will then examine (1) inflammation, through intravital microscopy which allows us to look at the bladder cells of live mice; (2) infection, through bacterial counts and (3) pain by studying the pain tolerance and behaviour of the mice.

column36: Access to Healthcare by Socially Vulnerable Persons during the COVID-19 Pandemic: An exploration of race and intersectionality
column37: Although the Canadian Medicare system was created to make sure that everyone has access to affordable healthcare, some people fall between the cracks. The Covid-19 pandemic has drawn attention to health and healthcare disparities that can't be ignored. In Montreal, Quebec, the largest number of Covid-19 cases are reported in neighborhoods with high rates of poverty and the most racial diversity. Although over 22% of the Canadian population identify as a non-white visible minority, unlike the USA, racial/ethnic differences in health and access to healthcare are not commonly discussed. In this study, we will explore the experiences of racialized minorities in accessing primary healthcare during the pandemic in multicultural neighborhoods in Montreal. We will talk with different racialized groups to understand their healthcare needs and challenges in accessing care and discuss our findings with family doctors to identify strategies to promote cultural safety and access. Without research that directly addresses race-based differences in the Canadian healthcare system, it is likely that the inequities in healthcare access that have been seen during the pandemic will continue.

column36: Engineering Expression of His-tag Labelled Proteins by Human Platelets
column37: Platelets are small, simple cells that play many roles in the body, from clotting to immune response. When they are made, platelets contain all the necessary cell machinery to make proteins. However, only a select few proteins seem to be made in platelets, and much about the necessary modifications and steps of protein production in platelets is unknown. Therefore, we wanted to express foreign proteins in platelets to help determine what protein production capabilities platelets have, and the necessary modifications for production to occur. To achieve this, we will encase the protein synthesis directions (mRNA) in incredibly small lipid systems, called lipid nanoparticles (LNPs). The LNPs will then protect the mRNA until it can be taken up into platelets and be translated into protein. The mRNA will encode for reporter proteins, to allow for easy visualization and detection, and contain modifications based off known proteins that are translated in platelets. Analyses to determine if the proteins have been made will be completed using several different techniques. In the future, modifications of platelet protein production could have many different clinical implications. ""Designer-platelets"" could be produced with enhanced functions, adding a layer of control to the role of platelets within a patient. For example, platelets transfused to treat acute or severe hemorrhage could be made to express additional clotting factors, enhancing their ability to stop bleeding. Additionally, in cancer treatments where platelets are already being transfused, protein expression would help target therapies to tumors, expanding the role of platelets into a new cell therapy.

column36: Machine learning-guided design of bio-orthogonal metallic nanoparticles for biosensing of urinary tract infection-causing bacteria
column37: Urinary tract infections (UTIs) are a highly prevalent communicable infectious disease caused predominantly by bacteria, with a higher incidence in women, children and the elderly. Due to the large variety of UTI-causing bacteria, the gold standard for diagnosis, urine culture and inspection, is a laborious and time-consuming procedure that can only be performed in equipped clinical laboratories. As a result, physicians often prescribe drugs based on clinical observations and error-prone screening tests, which can result in incorrect treatment, contribute to antibiotic resistance, and increase a patient's risk of developing health complications. Diagnostic platforms commonly use specific probes for each bacterial species being detected, where every probe can detect only one specific species. This requires multiple tests to be run, either in parallel or sequentially, to identify the disease-causing bacterial species – an inefficient approach for use at the point of care. Using machine learning, my project develops novel, ""bio-orthogonal"" metal nanoparticle probes for bacterial identification: an efficient diagnostic strategy relying on generalized sensing mechanisms. I will study how metal nanoparticles of different compositions, structures, and surface chemistries interact with bacteria through generalized mechanisms. All bacteria have similar features on their surface; however, the properties and arrangements of these features are unique to each species. By using machine learning, I will model the patterns of interaction between unique bacterial species and a given nanoparticle design. This model will then be used to select a single, optimal set of ""bio-orthogonal"" metal nanoparticle probes capable of identifying every UTI-causing bacterial species with a single test.

column36: Epigenome wide association of extracellular vesicle characteristics with frailty and accelerated aging in older women
column37: As our lifespan continues to increase, therapeutics that can increase healthspan become a dire need. To understand how to design such anti-aging therapeutics, my project will explore how biological age is transmitted between cells. Recent research has shown that aging-related diseases, such as loss of muscle and the decreased cell efficiency, are a result of changes in cell function over time. Given that this cell function is reflected by its genome, aging-related changes in our epigenome have been profiled to create epigenetic clocks-biomarker tools that predict biological age in association with mortality and disease. With the nature of aging occurring at the cellular level but being coordinated across the entire human, we believe that aging signals might be communicated via extracellular vesicles (EVs): small cell-derived messengers with a variety of cargo. Current literature suggests that both epigenetic changes and EVs are involved in the deterioration of cell efficiency with aging. Therefore, this NFRF-funded exploratory research project will use chronologically-matched paired samples from the WARM Hearts cohort to address three important questions: 1) how EV characteristics (i.e. size, origin, content, and enrichment) are associated with changes in the epigenome; 2) whether aging-related epigenetic marks are associated with frailty and aging-related disease; and 3) whether EVs do in fact participate in communicating biological age between cells. Altogether, my project will help us discover what epigenetic signals are being transmitted by EVs in the process of biological aging. The data we generate can ultimately be used to develop effective anti-aging therapeutics that decelerate/reverse aging, while identifying the onset of frailty and aging-related disease.

column36: The role of primitive neural stem cells in the functional recovery after neonatal brain injury
column37: Perinatal hypoxic/ischemic (H/I) insult is a prevalent cause of brain injury in infants. Children who suffer from this form of brain injury exhibit long-term neurological complications ranging from mild behavioural deficits to severe seizures, mental retardation, and/or cerebral palsy. Their care and management represent a significant long-term personal, familial, economic, and societal challenge for Canadians. With the exception of rehabilitation, there are currently no established treatments available to improve behavioral deficits in these patients and despite its prevalence and significant impact on the health care system, pediatric ischemia is largely unstudied. A promising therapeutic strategy is neural regeneration through the recruitment of resident neural stem cells that are responsive to drug treatment. Specifically, our lab has previously shown that the activation of resident neural stem and progenitor cells (together termed neural precursor cells, NPCs) using the FDA approved drug metformin, is sufficient to promote functional recovery in a model of neonatal H/I. In my proposed studies, I will focus on understanding the cellular basis for this observed recovery by determining whether neural stem cells are directly contributing to tissue repair. I hypothesize that resident NPCs and their progeny are activated in response to HI and metformin treatment, expand in number, migrate to the site of the injury and differentiate into neural phenotypes to replace lost cells. Elucidating this cellular mechanism will uncover novel targets for future therapeutics. Ultimately, this will promote the health of affected Canadians and reduce the socioeconomic burden on families and the healthcare system.

column36: Etude des variants pharmacogenetiques de la reponse au cannabis
column37: La prise d'un nouveau medicament comporte toujours son lot d'incertitudes. Est-ce qu'il sera efficace? Est-ce que j'aurai des effets secondaires? Il peut s'ecouler un certain temps avant que le medecin trouve la bonne combinaison entre le medicament et tous les facteurs qui influencent les reactions du corps vis-a-vis ce dernier. Parmi ces facteurs, on retrouve nos genes, dont certains sont connus pour dicter la reaction du corps a un medicament. Il serait possible d'ameliorer le delai pour atteindre l'efficacite souhaitee et d'eviter les effets secondaires d'un traitement. L'information sur nos genes impliques dans la reponse de notre corps a un medicament donne peut s'obtenir par des tests genetiques qui ne sont pas, a l'heure actuelle, entierement accessibles aux medecins. L'objectif de ce projet de recherche est d'etudier ces facteurs genetiques. Pour ce faire, nous etudierons le cannabis comme traitement des douleurs chroniques. Nous souhaitons identifier les genes qui expliquent pourquoi certaines personnes repondent moins bien au cannabis ou manifestent des effets secondaires importants comme les hallucinations, la dependance et les problemes de memoire. Pour ce faire, nous recruterons 150 participants qui presentent de la douleur chronique et qui utilisent du cannabis pour la soulager. Nos resultats pourraient permettre d'identifier des genes (marqueurs) qui modifient la reponse du corps au cannabis et d'utiliser cette information pour ameliorer l'efficacite et la securite du cannabis pour traiter des conditions de sante. Le but ultime est donc d'identifier ces marqueurs qui, un peu comme predire les resultats de la loterie avant le tirage nous aiderait a savoir si c'est le bon medicament pour le patient avant m eme de debuter le traitement.

column36: Screening for Mild Cognitive Impairment in Adults with Dual Sensory Impairment: Adaptation of MoCA for Face-to-Face and Remote Clinical Practice
column37: The cognitive functioning in people with sensory impairments (vision, hearing) declines more rapidly than in individuals without sensory impairments. However, these findings are not always well-known to many healthcare professionals in charge of cognitive screening. The Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) is one of the most widely used tools to screen for mild cognitive impairment. Yet, very few studies explore the development of an optimal protocol for its administration to people with sensory impairments. This project aims to bridge the gap between current knowledge and clinical practice by providing clinicians with appealing, engaging and accessible educational tools that will have a positive effect on their practice. The study objectives are to: (1) Synthesize the literature to understand the sensitivity measures currently used by clinicians when administering the MoCA to individuals with sensory impairment(s) by conducting a scoping review of the literature and (2) Effectively transfer essential knowledge from different specialists to clinicians to optimize the administration of the MoCA to individuals with sensory impairment(s) using an integrated knowledge translation approach. Educational materials on various aspects of sensory impairment, developed by researchers from the Canadian Consortium on Neurodegeneration in Aging (CCNA), will be disseminated to more than 5,000 participating clinicians across Canada. Upon completion of each module and six months later, the knowledge, attitudes and practices of the clinical participants will be assessed using questionnaires. Shaping appropriate diagnostic protocol measures will foster clinicians' confidence in their knowledge about the issue, their practice, thereby contributing to the well-being of their patients.
