Islet ultrastructure will be assessed with electron microscopy. Our experiments will provide a quantitative and qualitative analysis outlining the serial evolution of important molecules in the developing islets. This research will provide key information on the basic biology of pig islet development, which will help advance pig islet xenotransplantation towards utilization in the clinical world.

column36: The Effects of the Ketogenic Diet on Premature Aging in Major Depressive Disorder.
column37: Major depressive disorder (MDD) or simply depression affects around 20% of Canadians. Recently, studies have shown that MDD is linked with age-related diseases, such as cancer, diabetes, and heart disease. This has caused scientists to hypothesize that this mental condition might be linked to a process of accelerated aging. This was confirmed by studies that investigated signs of early aging in the DNA of MDD patients, such as the shortening of the extremities of chromosomes (telomeres), reduced telomerase activity, and changes in specific parts of the DNA (a process called DNA methylation). These are events that occur normally as one ages, though are commonly present earlier in life in individuals with MDD. Our project aims to investigate the effect of a ketogenic diet (KD) on successfully treating MDD and reducing the rate of premature aging. The KD is simply a high-fat, very low-carbohydrate diet. Many studies have shown the effect of a KD on successfully treating various mood disorders. The KD has appeared to improve age-related brain stability, and our project plans to investigate this effect on patients with MDD. Two patient groups will be studied; those solely on a KD diet, and another group who will be consuming a KD with carbs. After 12 weeks, we will determine reductions in MDD symptoms, and analyze patient blood for changes in the markers of early aging. Our project will determine the potential of the KD as a viable therapy for treatment resistant MDD patients and help us understand its effect on premature aging. It will help contribute to finding new and better treatment options for depression, using nutritional approaches. This method may be more accessible and affordable to many MDD patients, providing them with an effective choice of therapy.

column36: The efficacy of an apelin analog in ameliorating the pathophysiology of pulmonary arterial hypertension
column37: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a rare progressive syndrome in which lung arterial pressures and vascular resistance are elevated, leading to adverse blood vessel remodeling, and right heart failure which is often fatal. Existing treatments are ineffective hence an average survival time of 3 years from time of diagnosis. Studies have shown that the natural hormone, apelin, is downregulated in patients with PAH. Apelin is shown to have beneficial and protective properties for the blood vessels, inducing their relaxation, and promoting stronger heart contraction. Restoring the apelin pathway is promising in reversing blood vessel defects seen in the disease progression of PAH. However, the salutary actions of apelin are limited by its short half-life due to degradation by enzymes. Apelin analogs have been developed that extend their half-life to allow for evasion of degradation. Our project aims to evaluate the efficacy of an apelin analog in ameliorating the impairments seen in PAH using a rat model of PAH. Caged rats will be split into a control or PAH group. For 3 weeks, the control group will be kept in normal air while PAH rats will be kept in low oxygen and subcutaneously injected with a drug that induces lung injury, sugen, weekly. After, all groups will be kept in normal air for 5 weeks and receive daily apelin analog injections within the last 3 weeks. Echocardiography will be used to assess heart function and structure, and artery catheterization will be used to measure ventricular and blood flow parameters. Hearts and lungs will be removed to undergo histological analysis. We predict that apelin analog treatment will improve the cardiac function of rats exposed to sugen and low oxygen, preventing right heart failure while rescuing rat lung function.

column36: Evolution du statut clinique de patients atteints de la fibrose kystique avant le diagnostic du diabete : une etude de cohorte, de l'enfance a l'age adulte
column37: Au Canada, la fibrose kystique (FK) est la maladie hereditaire la plus frequente dans la population d'origine caucasienne, affectant jusqu'a une naissance sur 3600. Cette derniere atteint differents organes, dont principalement l'appareil digestif et les poumons, mais les patients atteints de FK decedent generalement d'insuffisance respiratoire suite a une maladie pulmonaire progressive. Le pancreas est aussi un organe frequemment atteint par la FK, contribuant a la maldigestion, la malabsorption et au risque eleve de carences nutritionnelles de m eme qu'aux anomalies de la tolerance au glucose. Dans les dernieres decennies, l'accroissement de l'esperance de vie dans cette population a contribue a l'augmentation de la prevalence de certaines comorbidites. Le diabete associe a la fibrose kystique (DAFK), qui atteint maintenant pres de 50 % des patients de plus de 30 ans, est la comorbidite extra-pulmonaire la plus courante de la FK. Sa survenue est toutefois liee a un mauvais pronostic : risque accru de retard de croissance, perte de poids et reduction de la fonction pulmonaire avant le diagnostic de DAFK, menant a l'augmentation du risque de mortalite de ces patients. Afin de mieux cibler les patients a risque pour optimiser leur prise en charge, il est capital de reconnaitre les facteurs de risque du DAFK. L'objectif de ce projet de recherche est de mieux comprendre l'evolution clinique des patients atteints de FK de l'enfance a l'age adulte avant le diagnostic de DAFK. Nos resultats pourraient nous permettre de cibler des facteurs de risque associes au DAFK et ainsi faciliter l'identification des patients a risque. Ultimement, ceci permettrait d'initier precocement un suivi et des interventions intensives afin de tenter de minimiser les impacts de cette comorbidite.

column36: Evaluating the effectiveness of small molecule modulators of circadian mechanism in improving cardiac outcome and immune responses post myocardial infarction

column36: The role of E-cadherin in the malignant progression of oral epithelial dysplasia
column37: The goal of this research is to predict which oral precancerous lesions (OPL) (changes in the mouth that are at risk of becoming cancer) will become cancer. The epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a process where epithelial cells, which are cells that protect and line our body, gain the traits of mesenchymal cells (such as travelling and invading other tissues or organs), thus playing a role in cancer development. One feature of EMT is the loss of E-cadherin, which is a protein that attaches epithelial cells to one another. E-cadherin is greatest in normal oral tissue but decreases as the tissue changes from normal to precancer to cancer. To date, there is no research on using E-cadherin to anticipate which OPLs will become cancer. In our research, we predict that early OPLs at greatest risk of progressing to cancer will show less E-cadherin than OPLs that do not progress to cancer. The British Columbia Oral Cancer Prevention Program (BC OCPP) has been following patients with OLPs for more than 20 years. Data and tissue samples from patients who participate in the BC OCPP's Oral Cancer Prediction Longitudinal Study will be used in our proposed research. column36: The role of the placenta in shaping heart and brain development
column37: The placenta is the crucial temporary organ that provides all nutrients to the growing baby during pregnancy. Placental defects often result in pregnancy complications such as miscarriage and preterm birth. The key function of the placenta as a nutrient and gas supply organ is well recognized, however, the placenta also directs development of specific organ systems. By using the mouse model, it has been demonstrated that placental defects can be the sole cause of congenital heart and neuro-developmental defects. Placental abnormalities are significantly correlated with heart defects in newborns and with autism spectrum disorders in children, which become more frequent in children to females of older age. Accordingly, my lab has shown that advanced maternal age commonly results in placental defects. Despite the impact the placenta has on heart and brain development, little is known about how they interact. My main hypotheses are that (1) shared master regulatory gene networks govern development of the placenta, heart and brain, and (2) that these networks are error prone in the placenta in mothers of advanced age. In Aim 1, I will analyze gene levels and define regulatory sequences in the placenta, heart and brain of mouse embryos. In Aim 2, I will determine the extent that these networks are affected in pregnancies to females near the end of their reproductive lifespan, and how the aging maternal environment impacts placental and embryonic development. This project will uncover the mechanisms that tie the placenta to normal formation of the heart and brain. The insights gained will be important to inform future analyses into the developmental origins of congenital defects, in particular those that become more prevalent in offspring to mothers of advanced age.

column36: Evaluating the impact of the 'Biosimilars Initiative' for rheumatic conditions in British Columbia
column37: British Columbia (BC) was the first Canadian province, and jurisdiction in North America, to institute a mandatory policy requiring individuals to be switched to biosimilars, 'Biosimilars Initiative for Prescribers'. As a result of this controversial policy, patients with rheumatic conditions (i.e. ankylosing spondylitis, plaque psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, or rheumatoid arthritis) were required to switch from innovator biologic drugs to less expensive biosimilar equivalents. This policy came into effect by November 2019; early estimates suggest BC may be saving $1.78 million per month from the switching policy. The objective of this research is to evaluate the policy's impact on drug use, adherence, healthcare utilization, and prescribing patterns using interrupted time series analysis (ITS). This project will utilize administrative data including BC PharmaNet, Medical Service Plan (MSP), Discharge Abstract Database (DAD), and National Ambulatory Care Reporting System (NACRS). The trainee hypothesizes that there will be increased biosimilar utilization, increased utilization of biologics with no biosimilar, no changes in adherence or healthcare utilization, and no difference in prescribing practices by geographic region or specialty after the 'Biosimilars Initiative' policy came into effect. The trainee will generate a cohort of individuals with the aforementioned rheumatic conditions. Subanalyses will be conducted according to important patient level characteristics, such as age, sex, area of residence, socioeconomic status, comorbidity burden, and polypharmacy. Prescribing patterns will be stratified by specialty and geographic location. The results of the proposed research are expected to inform the public, prescribers, and policymakers within BC and beyond.

column36: Assessment of Frailty in Older Patients Who Undergo Major Non-Cardiac Surgery
column37: Older adults are predisposed to suffering life-altering complications after surgery and strategies to mitigate these risks have shown inconsistent results. Part of the problem lies in that surgeons lack accessible tools to identify which patients are at risk of a poor outcome. Identifying high-risk patients prior to surgery is critically important as it guides informed consent and enables the prescription of therapy that is tailored to the individual. For example, multidisciplinary interventions such as nutritional supplementation and exercise training can be prescribed to patients before surgery when they are found to have reduced function and health, a medical state known as frailty. Recent studies have shown that frail older individuals are particularly vulnerable to stressors such as surgery. The objective of my project is to find feasible tools that can be used to detect frailty in older patients scheduled to have a major operation. In particular, I will focus on two novel tools that are simple to administer and require minimal resources: (1) hand grip strength, and (2) the time required to stand from sitting, walk 3 meters, and return to sitting (also known as Timed-Up-and-Go). To investigate the value of these tools, I will capitalize on data from an ongoing study of older patients having surgery in 12 hospitals across Canada. If I can demonstrate that simple physical tests such as hand grip strength and Timed-Up-and-Go can be used to identify frailty, surgeons across the country could readily implement these tools in their clinical practice. This information will guide resource allocation on targeted therapies for those who are most likely to benefit around the time of surgery.

column36: Understanding the impact of bowel dysfunction on quality of life in rectal cancer patients
column37: Patient-centred care requires outcomes that are relevant to patients. Bowel dysfunction is an important consequence of surgery for rectal cancer, and although there are many studies investigating the effect bowel function after rectal cancer surgery on quality of life (QOL) almost all of these studies use generic QOL instruments. These instruments may neglect concepts important to patients with bowel dysfunction after rectal cancer surgery. Given these limitations, counselling patients regarding their surgical treatment options may be affected. The objectives of this project are to identify the QOL domains that are important to patients after rectal cancer treatment and then apply these findings to evaluate current evidence, guide further research and better advise patients regarding their treatment options. This will be completed by evaluating bowel dysfunction and decisional regret in patients after rectal surgery. We will subsequently conduct patient interviews to identify important concepts to patients. We will then use this data to evaluate current literature and properly convey the outcomes and potential impacts of bowel dysfunction or a permanent stoma to patients following rectal cancer treatment. These results will help inform the development of a patient-centred decisional aid by focusing on the specific QOL domains that are affected by bowel dysfunction and a permanent colostomy. In addition, the results of these studies will also help clinicians measure and interpret bowel dysfunction and QOL changes in rectal cancer patients by identifying important outcomes from the patient's perspective and identify the QOL instruments have the most content validity in this context. Ultimately, our study aims to evaluate patient-centred outcomes in rectal surgery.

column36: Placental disease subtypes as predictors of aortic stiffness, endothelial dysfunction and adverse arterial hemodynamics in women with preeclampsia
column37: Preeclampsia (PE) is a disease of pregnancy characterized by high-blood pressure after 20-weeks gestation. PE is associated with a 12-fold increase in risk for cardiovascular disease (CVD). Previous research has revealed 3 subtypes of PE each associated with distinct placental pathology lesions. For my thesis, I propose a research project that explores potential associations between PE subtypes and arterial health. My research question is: Placental disease subtypes as predictors of aortic stiffness, endothelial dysfunction and adverse arterial hemodynamics in women with preeclampsia. I plan to recruit 35 PE and 5 healthy control participants from a pre-existing cohort. A placenta histopathology evaluation will be completed for each participant. This evaluation will indicate the presence and severity of 30 placental lesions. The PE-subtype of each participant can then be determined using a machine learning algorithm with a >75% accuracy. Next, participants will complete an arterial health assessment which will characterize their arterial stiffness, hemodynamic load and endothelial function. These measures are predictors for future CVD. The association between PE subtype and measures of arterial health will be assessed by multivariable linear regression. The aim of this project is to identify PE subtypes that are associated with an increased risk for CVD. This could lead to the development of a novel, evidenced-based triage strategy where patients with high-risk PE subtypes can be identified at delivery and referred to post-partum CVD screening clinics and intervention. Currently there are no triage strategies. Based on the quantity of patients diagnosed with PE, >20,000 Canadians per year, a triage strategy is warranted to alleviate the burden on our healthcare system.

column36: Effet de la Perte de Poids Induite par la Chirurgie Bariatrique sur la Recompense Alimentaire et le Controle Cognitif : Etude Longitudinale en Imagerie par Resonance Magnetique Fonctionnelle (IRMf)
column37: L'obesite est une maladie neurocomportementale souvent associee a une atrophie cerebrale des regions reliees au controle cognitif ainsi qu'a une augmentation de la reponse cerebrale des regions impliquees dans la recompense et la valeur attribuee aux aliments. Les mecanismes expliquant ces changements ne sont pas elucides. De plus, il n'est pas clair si ces changements sont reversibles apres une perte de poids. La chirurgie bariatrique, un traitement efficace entrainant une perte de poids significative, induit une diminution des preoccupations envers la nourriture et des changements au niveau des preferences alimentaires. Quelques etudes d'imagerie par resonance magnetique (IRM) ont evalue les effets de la perte de poids induite par la chirurgie bariatrique sur la fonction et la structure du cerveau. Cependant, ces etudes etaient effectuees a court terme et comprenaient peu de participants. Nos objectifs sont donc de caracteriser les changements de la fonction cerebrale en reponse a des stimuli alimentaires dans des regions associees a la recompense et au controle cognitif, soit 4, 12 et 24 mois apres la chirurgie bariatrique de type gastrectomie parietale, et d'examiner les predicteurs neuronaux de la perte de poids 24 mois apres la chirurgie. Nous recrutons actuellement 50 individus severement obeses admis pour une gastrectomie parietale. a chaque rencontre, nous evaluons l'activite cerebrale par IRM fonctionnelle et les comportements alimentaires a l'aide de questionnaires. Nous emettons l'hypothese que la chirurgie induit une diminution de la sensibilite a la recompense alimentaire et une augmentation du controle de soi. Cette etude permettra de mieux comprendre les changements fonctionnels du cerveau en reponse aux aliments dans un contexte de perte de poids.

column36: Perceptions of intensive care nurses on their preparedness and coping during the COVID-19 pandemic
column37: Since the start of the COVID-19 pandemic, there have been an average of 471 active daily hospitalizations in Quebec, with an average of 21.2% of these hospitalizations requiring admission to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Namely, lack of preparedness in the context of global pandemic is associated with increased stress and more coping challenges. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to understand the experience of ICU nurses during the COVID-19 pandemic to better understand the effects of their preparedness on stress and coping. Nurses working in a designated COVID-19 ICU will be invited for individual qualitative semi-structured interviews held over Zoom Pro. Interview questions will relate to their preparation to offer care during a pandemic, their psychological well-being and their coping process. Self-reported stress-related symptoms will be evaluated using validated questionnaires. Data integration of interviews and questionnaires will determine the effects of preparedness on stress and coping experiences in ICU nurses. Study findings will guide service delivery planning during the COVID-19 pandemic and for subsequent pandemic management.

column36: Social Isolation and Depression Among Older Adults during the COVID-19 Pandemic and Beyond
column37: COVID-19 has caused many disruptions to our daily lives. One of the most significant is to our ability to be with our family, friends, and community. The older adults in our community have been designated as one of the most at-risk groups when it comes to the virus and, as a result, they are the ones we try most diligently to protect. This protection, however, comes at a cost and that cost is social isolation. Social distancing orders are a harsh blow to older adults who are already the most likely among us to live on their own. Research has shown that isolation can be as bad for your health as smoking, but it is a necessary evil in our present moment. One of the knock-on effects of social isolation during this pandemic has proven to be depression. Although it may well be justified, it could be argued that are we opting to protect the physical health of older adults at the expense of their mental health. Fortunately, there have been astonishingly rapid advances in the development and approval of COVID-19 vaccines and it appears they are just over the horizon, but will vaccines also ""cure"" the depression caused by social isolation? This work will investigate the longer-term, post-pandemic effects on the mental health of older adults who have weathered the months-long stay-at-home orders by asking: Will increases in rates of depression among older adults persist beyond the lifting of social restriction orders and if so, who is most at risk for developing long-term problems?

column36: The role of PEX13 and PEX14 in lipid storage by coordinating peroxisomes with lipid droplets
column37: We are made up of trillions of cells where each contain various chemical micro-factories called organelles that specializes in its function. One of these organelles, the lipid droplet (LD), functions to store and supply fat molecules. These fat molecules act as raw materials in other organelles such as peroxisomes that make components necessary for our organs to function properly. Unfortunately, about 1/40000 babies are born with defects in genes that control peroxisome production and suffer from severe mental disabilities and shortened lifespan that have no effective treatments. These symptoms occur as a buildup of toxic fat molecules that are not processed by peroxisomes and depletion of other downstream molecules used by other organelles. By using fruit flies, we have identified that two of those genes involved in peroxisome production are also important for proper LD function. I have also found that one of them may function variably at the LDs for different peroxisome-deficient patients, which may cause different raw fat materials to build up or deplete. In fact, it was shown using a specific peroxisome-deficient fruit flies that supplementing depleted fat molecules in diet improved a neurological condition and improved survival rate while supplying them with an unaffected fat molecule worsened its lifespan. We will investigate whether these two newly identified genes have a role in deciding which fat molecules to accumulate or be depleted in different peroxisome-deficient flies. We will validate it by feeding them with different fat materials to see any positive or negative changes in their physiological conditions. This study may lead to personalized treatments for different peroxisome defective patients by varying nutrient options and drug-targeting genes.

column36: Solving the mystery of a rare neurodevelopmental disorder
column37: Approximately 3 million Canadians suffer from rare diseases, over half of which are children. Most people with these rare conditions, however, do not have diagnoses or treatments. Our research team has identified a group of patients in Canada and the U.S. with a rare neurological disorder which has not yet been reported. These patients have cognitive and walking impairments, as well as problems with sight and smell, suggesting they may suffer from abnormal brain development. Our collaborative team has identified mutations in the USP15 gene that are shared amongst our cohort of patients. Interestingly, mutations in this gene have recently been identified in different patients with autism spectrum disorder. How the gene affects brain development, however, is shrouded in mystery. We plan to use a combination of cell biology, mouse genetics, and biochemical approaches to determine: 1. How USP15 regulates brain development, and 2. how this mutation disrupts the ability of the brain to function properly. My study will uncover the uncharacterized mechanism behind this disorder and advance our understanding of the gene's role in brain development. Through understanding this rare disease, we hope to develop treatments that can improve their quality of life.

column37: Type 2 diabetes is a multifactorial condition with high prevalence in Canada. One of the severe complications of type 2 diabetes is impaired wound healing responses. Normally, the skin healing involves four steps which are: hemostasis, inflammatory phase, proliferative phase, and phase of maturation. However, in individuals with type 2 diabetes, this healing is impaired. Another common complication of type 2 diabetes is peripheral neuropathy which is characterized by a loss of motor and sensory axons, chronic pain, and a loss of sensation. Schwann cells regulate many aspects of axonal health and repair, so that disruption of their metabolism by diabetes results in the accumulation of neurotoxic intermediates and compromises production of neuronal support factors, contributing to axonal degeneration. Following skin injury, cutaneous axons are damaged which causes the activation of Schwann cells which migrate into the healing skin and help repair the dermis. Based on this: I hypothesize that in diabetic skin which suffers from peripheral neuropathy, Schwann cell activity is impaired which contributes to poor wound healing. To test this, I will use two common mouse models of diabetes, the db/db mouse and high-fat diet feeding (HFD). We will induce a wound in the back skin and track how it heals. Additionally, we will count the number and assess the activity of Schwann cells, nerves, and vasculature. Next, we will try to rescue the defect in wound healing by taking two approaches. First, we will transplant healthy Schwann cells to attempt to stimulate wound closure and second, to apply growth factors which we have previously defined to be secreted by Schwann cells. Collectively, these experiments aim to test a novel therapeutic strategy to treat non-healing diabetic wounds.

column36: Contributors to Walking Capacity Among Older Adults with Multiple Sclerosis
column37: Background Walking impairments are one of the most prevalent and disabling symptoms experienced by older adults with MS. Exercise interventions have shown to have small but beneficial effects on walking capacity however, an age-specific exercise prescription has not yet been established for older adults with MS and walking impairments. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to inform exercise interventions and rehabilitation programs by identifying target physiological fitness parameters (e.x. muscular strength and cardiorespiratory fitness) that contribute towards walking capacity in older adults with MS. Objectives This study will examine the correlation between fitness parameters (muscular strength, power and endurance of the lower limbs and hips, and aerobic fitness) and walking speed and endurance in older adults with MS. Methods 20 older adults with MS (age 50 or over) and 20 healthy controls matched for age and sex will undergo a neurological exam, muscular and aerobic fitness assessments and measurements of walking speed and endurance. Significance The specific exercise prescription for older adults with MS and walking impairments is restricted due to an incomplete understanding of the fitness parameters that contribute to walking capacity. The results from this study will inform future exercise interventions improving walking capacity and quality of life and thus reducing fall and fracture risk in older adults with MS.

column36: Impaired clearance of dead and dying cells: pain and joint outcomes in knee osteoarthritis patients.
column37: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common joint disease, yet no disease-modifying treatment is available and the underlying pathological mechanisms that lead to joint failure are not well understood. OA is typically characterized as the breakdown of cartilage within the joint, however, inflammation within the joint is now also recognized as a hallmark of the disease. A subtype of cells that are part of the immune system, known as macrophages, play an important role in maintaining a healthy synovium-tissues that line the inside of joints. The Appleton lab has recently discovered that a fundamental role of macrophages-efferocytosis; clearing dead/dying cells-is impaired when exposed to synovial fluid from knee OA patients. However, it remains unknown if impaired efferocytosis leads to worse OA outcomes as well as how inflammation affects synovial macrophage function. Firstly, we want to test the effect of inhibiting the clearance of dead and dying cells on pain and joint tissue outcomes in a rat model of OA. A surgical procedure will be performed on rats to simulate knee OA followed by injection of chemical agents that impair macrophage function within the synovium. Subsequent joint damage and pain behaviour will be assessed through tissue imaging and pain measurements, respectively. Secondly, we want to compare macrophage function between human patients with low versus high levels of inflammation. Samples of patient synovium will be collected to measure macrophage clearance activity and efficiency. Overall, our research project is of high clinical significance because an inability of macrophages to clear dead and dying cells within the synovium would likely result in poorer health of the joint and therefore worse outcomes for OA patients.

column36: Is resistance training similarly effective in overweight men and women at reversing markers of early onset sarcopenia?

Resistance training is an effective intervention to stimulate skeletal muscle hypertrophy in several healthy and clinical populations, and it may potentially delay the onset of sarcopenia in overweight adults. Significance: This proposed study will provide novel information on the potential sex-differences present in myofibre adaptions to resistance training in overweight, middle-aged adults. column36: Using longitudinal motor mapping and an automated skilled reaching paradigm to characterize motor impairment and recovery in a mouse model of cerebral microinfarction
column37: A common motor impairment following focal stroke is hemiparesis of the contralateral upper limb which reduces the ability of impacted individuals to perform activities of daily living. Although there have been various studies on motor impairments and recovery following focal stroke, little is known about how microinfarcts, or microscopic lesions, impact motor function. Cerebral microinfarcts are a common pathological finding in individuals over the age of 65, thus investigating their impact on motor function is critical. To accomplish this, we will combine a novel method of longitudinal skilled reaching assessment with optogenetics-based motor mapping to study the impact of microinfarcts within the motor system. Specifically, our recently developed home-cage automated skilled reaching apparatus (HASRA), will allow us to test over 20 mice/day with minimal experimenter input. To induce microinfarction, fluorescent microspheres are injected into the common carotid artery leading to the occlusion of microvasculature in a random pattern similar to the distribution of microinfarcts in humans. After investigating motor impairments, the HASRA system will be used to determine the most therapeutically effective rehabilitative method for inducing recovery of motor impairments. It is anticipated that motor maps will be disrupted and skilled reaching impaired following microinfarction, but it is predicted that these impairments will be ameliorated through rehabilitative training in the HASRA system. Overall, this will be the first rodent study to evaluate skilled motor impairments following diffuse microinfarction and our results will shed light on the nature of motor deficits that are observed in some patients with microinfarcts.

column36: Effects of common footwear on gait mechanics in individuals with lower-limb amputations

column36: Defining the link between viral co-infection and the invasive potential of Neisseria meningitidis
column37: Neisseria meningitidis (Nme) is a species of bacteria that commonly live within the human throat. The danger of this bacteria lie in its potential to invade the bloodstream, causing the invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) that manifests in the form of sepsis and meningitis. Approximately 10% of IMD cases are fatal and the disease leaves a further 11-19% of patients with lifelong morbidities. Despite its importance, the trigger for Nme transitioning from harmlessly residing in the throat to invading into the bloodstream is not understood. Observations from the United States and several African countries suggest a strong correlation between the flu season and the incidence of IMD. In this study, I plan to examine the role of the influenza A virus (IAV) in augmenting the ability of Nme to invade the bloodstream, using transgenic mouse models that express human genes. Nme is a human-specific pathogen, meaning that its bacterial machinery has been optimized to infect humans only and it cannot infect mice. To circumvent this problem, I will be using mice that express human-specific genes that are suggested to affect Nme colonization in humans. These mice will be infected with Nme to examine the role of the human factors in asymptomatic infection and disease. Furthermore, the mice will be concurrently infected with IAV and Nme, and the immune responses to the infections and disease outcomes will be characterized. column36: Identifying the role of stress granules in the pathogenesis of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis using spatial proteomics
column37: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis is a fatal neurodegenerative disease characterized by the widespread death of motor neurons throughout the central nervous system. An estimated 80% of patients die within 5 years of onset and in over 90% of cases there lacks any discernible cause. Progress towards a cure, however, is derailed by our poor understanding of the disease at the molecular level. Nonetheless, a growing body of evidence has intimately linked the pathogenesis of ALS to aberrant changes in stress granules (SGs). SGs are transient, stress-induced organelles that are critical for RNA metabolism. However, aberrant changes in SG dynamics have been repeatedly linked to ALS pathogenesis. As SGs harbour over 450 proteins, understanding disease relevant changes in SG dynamics will require systematic profiling of the proteomic changes that occur in ALS genetic contexts. To this end, my project will study the impact of ALS-causing genes on SG dynamics and protein aggregation; and utilize high-resolution spatial proteomics to catalog the proteomic changes underlying these effects. My research aims to discover the mechanism underlying SG contributions to ALS pathogenesis and to further elucidate the biological underpinnings of ALS.

column36: Effet de l'activation des astrocytes du noyau sensoriel principal du Trijumeau sur la rythmogenese de la mastication
column37: Les mecanismes par lesquels le systeme nerveux programme les mouvements rythmiques vitaux comme la mastication, la respiration et la locomotion sont encore mal connus. Ces fonctions sont programmees par des reseaux de neurones qui generent une commande rythmique a transmettre aux muscles. Nous avons identifie une population de neurones, dans un noyau du tronc cerebral, capables de produire une activite rythmique que l'on croit responsable des mouvements de la mastication. Nos travaux ont aussi demontre que les astrocytes, un type de cellules gliales, sont essentiels pour la genese de cette activite rythmique, ce qui est tres different des fonctions normalement attribuees aux astrocytes. Or ces donnees ont toutes ete obtenues in vitro. L'objectif de ce projet est de valider in vivo grace a l'optogenetique l'implication des neurones et des astrocytes du noyau du tronc cerebral dans la genese des mouvements masticatoires. L'optogenetique est une technologie permettant de faire exprimer des proteines sensibles a la lumiere par des populations de cellules ciblees genetiquement. Ces proteines peuvent ensuite activer ou inhiber les cellules quand on les illumine avec la bonne longueur d'onde ou encore elles peuvent emettre un signal lumineux lorsque les cellules sont actives. Nous aurons recours a des souris transgeniques exprimant ces differentes proteines dans lesquelles nous implanterons des fibres optiques pour illuminer les astrocytes du noyau du tronc cerebral ou encore pour detecter leur activite pendant la mastication chez l'animal eveille. Si des resultats concluants sont obtenus, ceci sera la premiere demonstration in vivo que l'activation des astrocytes produit un comportement moteur coherent et coordonne.

column36: The role of B cells in blood pressure regulation and hypertension
column37: Hypertension (HTN) is a disease that affects one third of the adult population. The development of HTN has traditionally been attributed to dysfunctions of the kidneys, blood vessels, or imbalances of specific hormones in the body. Recently however, there is growing interest about the role of the immune system in blood pressure (BP) control and HTN, but how this occurs is not fully understood. Our lab has shown that B cells, a type of immune cell, are important for BP control: genetically-modified mice born with permanent B cell deficiency have lower BP than normal mice. They also have increased urinary sodium and water excretion (which is known to decrease BP) and reduced expression of vasopressin receptor-2 (V<sub>2</sub>R), a kidney protein that promotes sodium and water retention. We hypothesize that B cell deficiency reduces kidney V<sub>2</sub>R expression, which elevates sodium and water excretion, and lowers blood volume and BP. In this project, we will examine if B cells causally affect BP through alterations in kidney function using a mouse model in which B cells are only depleted after giving diphtheria toxin injections. We will examine if these mice develop decreased BP due to elevated sodium and water excretion, and whether they are resistant to experimental HTN. We also aim to explore the molecular mechanism by which this occurs. Computational analyses suggest that V<sub>2</sub>R expression in the kidneys is initiated by the NF-kB signalling pathway, a commonly used mechanism in immune cells. Our preliminary data has shown activation of the NF-kB pathway by B cell-produced factors, suggesting regulation of V<sub>2</sub>R by B cells. Understanding how B cells control BP and kidney function would help us identify new causes of HTN, and possibly lead to HTN treatments that target B cells.

Using the baculovirus expression system, the Gotte lab has been able to express the polymerase complex, allowing us to explore potential inhibitors. Using polyacrylamide gel electrophoresis (PAGE), I will be screening potential inhibitors. I will be determining the concentration required to inhibit 50% of activity and also exploring the specificities of the inhibitors. If there is a compound that shows promise, we will study it in cell culture as well as determine the mechanism of action. I believe that my research will contribute significantly to the fight against coronavirus.

column36: Investigating the Neural Correlates of Reward Processing in Children of Parents with Cannabis Use Disorder
column37: Altered reward processing in the ventral striatum and medial prefrontal cortex during anticipatory processing is linked to poor decision-making, particularly in the context of substance use disorders (SUDs). Specifically, individuals with cannabis use disorder (CUD) show blunted neural activation during anticipatory reward processing. Still, very little is known about potential inherited vulnerability through parental cannabis use on children. The monetary incentive delay task (MIDT) is a widely used task to assess the neural correlates of reward and loss processing. During the anticipation phase of the MIDT, individuals with CUD have shown divergent activity in the ventral striatum and medial prefrontal cortex compared to controls. The objective of this study is to investigate the neural correlates of reward processing in children of parents with CUD, compared to controls without a family history of CUD. The proposed study will assess performance on the MIDT while participants undergo functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Specifically, the study will examine if parental family history of CUD is related to altered neural activations during reward processing in children. The proposed study will analyze data previously collected from the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development (ABCD) Study, one of the largest studies using an open science model to longitudinally examine brain development in children through to adolescence. The proposed study will be a novel investigation of reward processing in youth at-risk for SUDs, prior to initiation of substance use. The findings will enhance our knowledge on factors that influence reward processing in the developing brain.

column36: Targeting the pro-metastatic function of cancer-associated fibroblasts in breast cancer: the promise of inhibiting the MNK/4E signaling axis
column37: In Canada, breast cancer alone accounts for approximately 13% of all deaths in women due to cancer. Up to 90% of these deaths do not occur due to the initial tumor, but from the secondary growths that travel from the primary site to distant organs (process of metastasis). One strategy employed by cancer is the dysregulation of normal protein production, allowing it to more easily adapt and gain the ability to spread throughout the body. Knowledge of this dysregulation process is limited to what happens within cancer cells only. However, a tumor is composed of cancer cells as well as non-cancerous stromal cells. It is known that cancer re-educates these surrounding stromal cells, resulting in a change of behaviour that is supportive of tumor growth and progression. My project focuses on these stromal cells and the role that protein production dysregulation in them plays in assisting cancer progression. To research this, I will focus on a molecule called eIF4E (an integral piece of the protein production machinery) in a re-educated stromal cell called cancer associated fibroblasts (CAFs). CAFs facilitate tumor growth and invasion by suppressing the immune system and redesigning the surrounding tissue, but eIF4E's contribution is unknown. A combination of cell culture experiments and mouse breast cancer models will be employed to ascertain its contribution, with a focus on whether eIF4E inhibition is effective in blocking breast cancer metastasis. The data gathered through this study is expected to help shape the pre-clinical therapeutic models being designed to better treat patients with breast cancer. For example, it will directly impact our recently funded Stand Up 2 Cancer trial, testing inhibitors of faulty protein production in women with metastatic breast cancer.

column36: The Effect of a Physical Activity Intervention on the Physical Activity Levels and Body Composition of Children with Congenital Heart Disease
column37: Congenital heart disease (CHD) is among the world's leading birth abnormalities. Improvements in detection and treatment mean more of these children will have longer lifespans. Despite the promising improvement in the length of their life, children with CHD are alarmingly inactive and face a number of short-term and long-term health challenges. Although children with CHD were previously restricted from participating in physical activity due to the fear of exacerbating their condition, it is now recommended that these children follow the same physical activity guidelines as their healthy peers. As such, physical activity may provide a method to encourage short- and long-term health and wellness. However, currently there is a lack of physical activity programs for children with CHD. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to evaluate the effect of an eight-month physical activity program on the physical activity levels and body composition of children with CHD. Forty children with CHD, between the ages of 7-17 will participate in the study. Twenty children will begin the program immediately while the remaining 20 participants will begin the program eight months later. The program will focus on increasing physical activity with the use of both aerobic and resistance training exercises. Physical activity levels and body composition (fat and lean mass) will be measured both before and after the eight-month program. The new knowledge gained from this study will provide a better understanding of the effects of physical activity on the body composition and health of children with CHD.

column36: Mental health of bariatric surgery patients
column37: In Quebec, 5% of adults suffer from severe obesity, which is known to have adverse consequences on physical and psychological health. Notably, it is associated with the development of chronic diseases, such as type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases and respiratory diseases. The recommended treatment for severe obesity is bariatric surgery. While this procedure is generally associated with a clinically significant weight loss, almost 50% of bariatric patients experience suboptimal post-surgical outcomes, like insufficient weight loss and/or consistent and rapid weight regain, even in the short term (i.e., within 6 months to 3 years post-surgery). The reasons remain poorly understood. One of the possible involved factors is mental health, which is a major risk factor for unhealthy eating and is not treated by surgery. The proposed study has two objectives: to assess the mental health of patients before and after bariatric surgery and to determine the impacts of mental health on the surgery outcomes. A total of 1000 participants awaiting surgery will be recruited. They will answer a questionnaire on their medical and sociodemographic history as well as questionnaires assessing psychiatric disorders, psychological distress and quality of life. We will also collect information in the medical record regarding their body mass index. All measurements will be taken 6 months pre-surgery and 6- and 12-months post-surgery. This study will determine the prevalence and impact of psychological factors on post-bariatric surgery weight loss and quality of life outcomes. The interventions that will be developed using these data will serve to improve the quality of life of patients while reducing government spending in the fight against obesity.

column36: Investigating the genetic background of rapid eye movement (REM)-sleep behaviour disorder to predict alpha-synucleinopathies
column37: Parkinson's disease, dementia with Lewy bodies, and multiple systems atrophy are collectively known as αlpha-synucleinopathies, which are characterized by aggregation and accumulation of αlpha-synuclein. Neurodegeneration at the time of diagnosis is irreversible, resulting in poor prognosis and failed outcomes in clinical trials. The majority individuals with rapid-eye-movement (REM)-sleep behaviour disorder (RBD) later develop alpha-synucleinopathies, providing potential for an earlier diagnosis. Advances in genomic approaches such as high-throughput sequencing have grown rapidly over the last few decades, and allow for a cost-effective and comprehensive investigation of the underlying genetic background in disease phenotypes. This research proposal offers the use of these tools to investigate the genetic background of RBD and its overlap with the genetic backgrounds of αlpha-synucleinopathies. Gene-based burden analyses will be conducted on whole genome sequencing (WGS) data from patients and controls to investigate the accumulation of rare variants in one of the cohorts compared to the others. Genes with the most accumulation of variants will then be sequenced in additional RBD samples and controls. Copy number variant analyses on WGS data cohorts will be performed, followed by association and regression tests to assess whether the variants are associated with increased or reduced risks of developing RBD and the three αlpha-synucleinopathies. The identification of candidate genes and their variants in RBD and αlpha-synucleinopathies will facilitate understanding of the mechanisms and genetic background underlying these neurodegenerative diseases, potentially allowing for earlier diagnoses and improved clinical trial outcomes for neuroprotective therapies.

column36: Elucidating Interactions Between Emotion Processing and Cognitive Control in Depression
column37: Major depressive disorder (MDD) is a mood disorder which affects more than 264 million people globally, placing a burden on both the individual and the society in which they live. Negative cognitive biases are a primary feature of MDD, where there is an increased attention and memory for negative emotional stimuli. Although emotion-processing centres of the brain, such as the amygdala, and cognitive-control regions, such as the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC), have been implicated in these negative cognitive biases, there is a lack of research into the interactions between these two regions, and how this interaction may be giving rise to negative cognitive biases. The objective of this research project will therefore be to elucidate the interactions between these regions of the brain, by not only investigating the amygdala and the DLPFC, but also the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). The ACC is a brain region which mediates the interactions between the amygdala and DLPFC, and has a dorsal cognitive-processing region, and a ventral emotion-related region. This will be done by having participants with MDD and matched controls complete a task which engages both the emotional and cognitive regions of the brain, while their level of brain activity within these regions of interest (amygdala, DLPFC, and ACC) are measured with functional magnetic resonance imaging. I hypothesize that higher levels of brain activity will be observed in the amygdala, DLPFC, and both the dorsal cognitive-processing and ventral emotion-related regions of the ACC. The results of this project will allow for a better understanding of the specific brain regions involved in negative cognitive biases, which will therefore help to improve the diagnosis and treatment of depression.

column36: Efficacy of heart failure treatments in diverse patient populations using induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes
column37: Heart failure plagues tens of millions of people annually, yet few treatment options are available to prevent a heart attack patient's condition from progressing to heart failure. Several currently approved drugs used for the medical management of heart failure have shown varying effects in patients. The extended time it takes to get patients on the right medication is detrimental to their health outcomes and contributes to a growing economic burden on the health care system. Clinical trials are often done on small populations without validating the drug efficacy in subpopulations such as in women, minorities, or the elderly, all of whom may react differently to the treatment. A new method of evaluating drug effectiveness in diverse patient populations is needed. This project will test the effectiveness of heart failure drugs in different demographic populations using patient-specific heart cells generated from blood samples. I will collect patient blood samples, reprogram them into cells with the potential to develop into many different cell types, otherwise known as stem cells, and then transform them into heart cells, called cardiomyocytes. Once cardiomyocytes are generated, we will induce a heart attack in these cells before treating them with currently available drugs. We will then analyze whether patient demographics, such as sex, race, and age, are predictors for these drugs' effectiveness since this is an important aspect of precision medicine. Additionally, this study will demonstrate the potential of patient-specific stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes for personalized drug-screening before prescribing heart failure drugs. Ultimately, this project seeks to improve patient health outcomes by prescribing them the most effective medication after a heart attack.

column36: Caracterisation de l'alimentation des femmes presentant une obesite dans un contexte d'infertilite
column37: L'infertilite est un probleme croissant qui affecte pres de 15% des couples au Canada. Parmi les causes d'infertilite, on retrouve l'obesite chez la femme. Cette situation nuit non seulement aux chances de concevoir naturellement mais engendre egalement une diminution de l'efficacite des traitements coûteux de fertilite. La presence d'obesite pourrait toutefois etre modifiee par un changement au niveau des habitudes de vie, notamment au niveau de l'alimentation. L'objectif du projet sera donc d'evaluer la qualite alimentaire de plus de 600 femmes presentant une obesite, recrutees dans sept cliniques de fertilite au Canada pour l'etude Ferti-Sante. Celle-ci vise a comparer les effets d'une intervention axee sur les saines habitudes de vie a ceux de la procreation assistee sur la fertilite de la femme. Les donnees sur l'alimentation seront recoltees au moyen d'un questionnaire de frequence alimentaire complete par les participantes au debut du projet. Il permettra de calculer les apports quotidiens en plus d'une centaine d'aliments, les apports totaux en chaque nutriment et un score de qualite alimentaire. Les apports nutritionnels des participantes seront ensuite compares aux recommandations canadiennes actuelles. Il sera ainsi possible d'evaluer l'incidence de pratiques alimentaires necessitant des ameliorations chez ce groupe. Qui plus est, cibler les problematiques nutritionnelles de cette population pourrait faire valoir la necessite d'une intervention conjointe en nutrition dans les cliniques de fertilite. Cette intervention pourrait a la fois augmenter les chances de conception et diminuer les coûts globaux associes a la procreation assistee, rendant ainsi accessible a beaucoup plus de femmes vivant un trouble de fertilite l'opportunite d'avoir une grossesse.

column36: Variability in Functional Brain Activity during Social Cognitive Processing in Schizophrenia Spectrum and Autism Spectrum Disorders
column37: Although autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD) appear markedly different, both involve social cognitive deficits and individual variability (heterogeneity) in brain activity. Impairments in social functioning are strong indicators of poor interpersonal and occupational outcomes in both disorders. Currently, very few studies have directly examined the neural circuitry of social cognition in both ASD and SSD, even though functional imaging studies have shown that both disorders display reduced activation of social processing regions. For my master's thesis, I will analyze data from a NIMH-funded harmonized multi-site, multi-study sample of social cognition and brain function in ASD/SSD (N>600), to (1) examine heterogeneity in SSD, ASD, and controls, and how this relates to the observed pattern of neurocognitive activity. I will (2) trans-diagnostically apply hierarchical clustering to further identify underlying neural activation pathways that lead to greater individual variability and a more 'idiosyncratic' response. Our study may provide new opportunities for targeted interventions such as brain stimulation, as well as guiding more biologically driven diagnostic markers. I will leverage this unique large sample harmonized dataset to uncover novel findings in neural circuit function and variability in SSD and ASD. This has implications for treatment innovation and current efforts which aim to expand beyond DSM-based diagnostic groups into transdiagnostic biologically based diagnoses.

column36: Sex-specific impact of the manipulation of methionine cycle on T cell activation and gut microbiome in neuroinflammation
column37: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease characterized by lesions in the brain and spinal cord in a context of aberrant activation of immune cells, especially pro-inflammatory T cells. Women are 3 times more affected by MS than men. The etiology of MS is unknown, but factors like obesity, diet and modification of the gut microbiota are associated with its clinical course. A commonly used model to understand immune mechanism in MS is the experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) in mice. Methionine is an amino acid that needs to be provided by food. In its cycle, methionine is converted by the enzyme Mat2a in S-adenosylmethionine (SAM), which is able to influence expression of genes. Our collaborator Dr Jones has shown that reducing methionine or inhibiting Mat2a decreases the proliferation of pro-inflammatory T cells. Our team showed that dietary methionine restriction (MR) is associated with a delay in apparition of neurologic symptoms and reduce activation and infiltration in the brain and spinal cord of these inflammatory immune cells in EAE, the mouse model of MS. Our preliminary results suggest that MR ameliorates EAE in both males and females but that the impacts are not identical. Our hypothesis is that the reduction of methionine improves inflammatory mechanisms in EAE by modifying the generation of pro-inflammatory immune cells and the composition of the gut microbiota in a sex-specific manner. With a transgenic mouse model, we also propose to study the inhibition of Mat2a and its impact on the T cells and the gut microbiota in EAE according to biological sex. The goal of this project is to understand the mechanisms through which MR delays and reduces neurological symptoms in EAE to open new tailored therapeutics avenues for women and men with MS.

column36: Trends and disparities in cervical cancer screening uptake in high HIV prevalence settings: a systematic analysis of population-based surveys in sub-Saharan Africa
column37: Cervical cancer (CC) is the 4th most common cause of cancer in women, and the leading cause of cancer death in women in sub-Saharan Africa (SSA). High income countries have witnessed dramatic reductions in CC burden due to implementation of vaccination programs against HPV, the causative agent of CC, alongside early detection (i.e. CC screening) and treatment strategies. Despite this, low- and middle-income countries continue to experience rising cases, most notably in SSA. Treatment and elimination of CC in SSA are further complicated by the presence of an HIV/HPV syndemic (synergistic epidemic). HIV/AIDS is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality in SSA and HPV co-infection exacerbates both viruses' impacts. Urgent action is needed to address this syndemic and reduce the rising incidence and mortality of this preventable disease. In August 2020, the WHO adopted a strategy for the elimination of CC by 2030. Improving our understanding of the current screening and treatment landscape is essential for the success of these efforts. The overarching goal of this thesis is to identify the longitudinal screening and uptake trends in SSA. Specifically, by: 1) Systematically analyzing large-scale population-based surveys to characterize trends in screening uptake and outcomes; and 2) Assessing disparities in screening uptake and outcomes by HIV status, socio-economic status, literacy, age, geography, marital status, and domestic violence experience. This will be achieved by analyzing health data from over 40 surveys using meta-analytic regression methods. Results of this project will be integrated into an established knowledge translation plan with international collaborators to ensure findings will be used to inform evidence-based initiatives to reach the WHO's goals.

column36: The Role of Nutrition in Muscle Function among Bariatric Surgery Patients
column37: Bariatric surgery procedures cause weight loss by restricting stomach size, ultimately leading to the malabsorption of nutrients. Despite this procedure's nature, the demand for bariatric surgery has increased 4-fold over the past 7 years in Canada, and it is alarming that current post-surgical nutritional recommendations are based on little to no research. In specific, evidence linked to protein intake is limited and is of concern, as protein plays a functional role in preserving fat-free mass, responsible for weight management, muscle function, and quality of life. Therefore, the proposed study will fill this gap by assessing post-surgical changes in protein intake/status and its effects on weight, body composition, energy metabolism, and muscle function. This study will follow a longitudinal, observational study design with an embedded qualitative approach. Fifty participants 18-50 years old will be recruited from the McGill University's Health Centre bariatric surgery clinic. Participants will be assessed pre-, 3-, and 6 months after surgery for weight, dietary intake, muscle function, body composition, energy expenditure, 24-h urine and blood parameters. In addition, 4 focus groups of 6-8 participants will be conducted at ≥ 3 months post-surgery.

column36: Perceived Social Support in Perinatal Populations During the COVID-19 Pandemic.
column37: During the perinatal period (pregnancy to 12 months postpartum), women experience increased vulnerability to anxiety and depressive disorders. This results in significant distress, impaired day-to-day functioning, and an increased risk of long-term emotional, behavioural, and physiological difficulties for their children. Recent findings suggest that prevalence rates of anxiety and depression may be even higher in the Canadian population during the current COVID-19 pandemic. Given the detrimental impact that a potential increase of anxiety and depressive disorders would have on both mothers and infants during the pandemic, it is crucial that research focuses on potential factors associated with the pandemic that may contribute to increases in such symptoms as well as affect the efficacy of treatment. Unfortunately, many Canadian women have experienced reduced social support as a result of the pandemic. Perceived social support (PSS) refers to individual's perception of the availability of social support and strongly predicts anxiety and depressive symptoms in women in the perinatal period. Further, PSS has been found to mediate the relation between interventions and clinical outcomes such as anxious and depressive symptoms. Thus, a reduction of PSS in the perinatal population during the COVID-19 pandemic may result in a reduction in treatment efficacy. The proposed study aims to explore the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on PSS in treatment seeking perinatal women and examine whether PSS mediates changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms following a CBT treatment group. Results from this novel study will further our understanding of how the COVID-19 pandemic has impacted the perinatal population and potentially inform the development of more efficacious interventions.

column36: Quantitative Analysis of the Evolution of Radiomic Feature Values in Simulated Positron Emission Tomography Images
column37: Cancer is one of the leading causes of death globally and accounted for about 9.6 million deaths in 2018. Extensive efforts from researchers to gain a better understanding of cancer have lead to the advancement of various medical imaging modalities and treatment methods. Medical imaging revealed distinct measurable characteristics between and within tumors that were later found to trigger adaptations in cancer cells for faster growth and resistance to treatment. Every tumor is different, and identifying the distinct characteristics in each tumor is crucial for modifying the treatment plan accordingly. Unfortunately, it is still unclear how these features are related to image properties in medical scans, tumor prognosis, and treatment outcomes. Radiomics is a method to quantitatively capture distinct tumor characteristics in medical images. Analysis of radiomic features provides information such as patterns, inter-pixel relationships, and textures in radiological images. Here we will use radiomics analysis to uncover how the features extracted from positron emission tomography (PET) imaging evolve with tumor growth. Movies of PET images will be acquired from my ongoing undergraduate thesis project on realistic tumor growth simulation. Radiomics analysis on these motion pictures will allow us to identify the most robust features that exhibit the most changes with tumor growth. These features will be optimal for tracking the disease progression and response to treatment. Successful identification of features can help design more sensitive image analysis methods that allows for personalized treatment for each cancer patient.

column36: Etude structure/fonction de l'activite d'une flavine monooxygenase dans la regulation de la cytokinese des cellules germinales chez C. elegans
column37: Nous etudions le phenomene de la division cellulaire, consistant en une cellule se divisant pour former deux cellules. La division cellulaire est un evenement crucial chez tous les etre vivants qui est souvent destabilise ou deregule dans les cellules cancereuses. Il est important de comprendre les mecanismes qui la regissent et pouvant faire defaut, entrainant la formation de cancers. Le syncytium est une structure formee lorsque la division cellulaire n'est pas complete et entraine la formation de deux cellules restant connectees entre elles. Cette structure est presente dans le developpement des cellules germinales, soit les cellules servant la reproduction, chez tous les animaux. Nous utilisons l'organisme modele C. elegans, un petit vers transparent et facile d'entretien, puisqu' il permet d'observer facilement au microscope les phenomenes se produisant dans les cellules. Ces observations menent a l' acquisition de donnees venant de l'analyse d'images, nous permettant de mesurer precisement ce que l'on observe. Mon projet vise a comprendre la fonction d'une nouvelle proteine decouverte chez C. elegans, qui semble impliquee dans la division cellulaire incomplete et la formation de syncytium. Cette proteine existe egalement chez l'humain, et pourrait etre impliquee dans certains types de cancers testiculaires. Cette enzyme, sa fonction et ses interacteurs dans la cellules ne sont pas bien connus a ce jour. Nos resultats preliminaires suggerent que cette proteine possede une fonction enzymatique, transferant une molecule d'oxygene a une proteine cible. L'etude de structure-fonction menee via mon projet permettra de mieux comprendre le role de cette proteine chez le vers, et ces resultats seront applicables a la comprehension de son role chez l'humain.

column36: Physical Activity among Immigrant and Non - Immigrant Youth: Findings from the Ontario Child Health Study
column37: A large and growing population of children and adolescents in Canada are foreign – born immigrants. Childhood obesity is a public health concern, with physical activity and healthy eating being recommended strategies. In Canada, the proportion of immigrant youth who are physically active is low, though the underlying reasons remain unclear. Previous literature has looked at mental health or socio-economic challenges as possible contributors, but this has not been fully examined in a Canadian setting. The purpose of this study is to compare levels of physical activity engagement between immigrant and non-immigrant youth. Secondly, it intends to assess the extent to which mental health, including mood and anxiety disorders, and socio-economic factors may explain these differences. The study will analyze data collected in the 2014 Ontario Child Health Study, which surveyed 10,802 children and adolescents in the province. The study contains data from the parent/guardian of the child or youth, youth self-report, and measures of physical activity, mental health, and lifestyle behaviours. Obesity is a significant risk factor for long-term cardiovascular outcomes. This study is a first attempt to understand the differences in physical activity among immigrant subgroups in Ontario, and the extent to which migrant status, mental health, and lifestyle behaviours may account for the differences. These findings will be useful for developing targeted interventions, taking into consideration other factors that may be barriers to achieving the recommended duration of physical activity.

column36: Characterizing age-related changes in the upper respiratory tract microbiome to reduce susceptibility of infection in older adults
column37: The upper respiratory tract (URT) contains an array of microbes that can contribute to or protect against upper respiratory infections (URIs). URIs in older adults increase risk of pneumonia and serious long-term health complications such as heart attack, dementia and increased risk of death. The increased risk of infection may be linked to the community composition and function of the URT microbiota. From a previous pilot study, nasal samples were collected from the anterior nares (nostril) region of healthy participants (20-100 years). Microbial composition and age-related changes were determined using 16S rRNA sequencing. Data indicated there are 5 major profiles of microbial communities and a potential loss of beneficial or protective microorganisms as age increases. We are currently collecting a cohort of nasal and saliva samples from healthy participants (20-100 years) to further understand how microbial composition changes with age, susceptibility to infection and seasonality, within the nasal and oral cavities. We have collected nasal swabs during Fall 2020 from the middle-turbinate (sinus) region from over 180 participants, with additional samples to be provided during Winter 2020 and Spring 2021. Currently, the samples are being processed with 16S rRNA sequencing to determine the composition and diversity changes within the URT microbiota of healthy participants. With the data collected from our pilot study and our current cohort, a computational analysis will be completed to further characterize microbial composition, diversity and age-related differences in the URT microbiota. These changes will identify protective microbial properties to develop novel therapeutic strategies, such as anti-infective agents to reduce the increased risk of URIs in older adults.

column36: Epigenetic Signatures of Childhood Developmental Outcomes in Relation to Parenting Quality
column37: There are few environmental factors that have as profound of an effect on child development as parenting. Especially during the vulnerable first few years of life, children are almost exclusively dependent on their caregivers to fulfill their basic needs and facilitate their social, emotional, and cognitive development. The link between parenting and childhood outcomes, such as cognitive performance or mental health, has been established but the underlying biology is only starting to be studied. While genetics (the DNA inherited from your parents) has been associated with these childhood outcomes, it has been suggested that another process called DNA methylation may have a role in the more dynamic relationship between childhood outcomes and parenting. DNA methylation is a type of alterable modification to DNA, which can vary throughout the lifecourse and has been shown to mediate the interaction between 'society' and 'cell'. Interestingly, foundational studies in mice and humans have shown that the parenting behaviours of newborns have been associated with changes at DNA methylation sites that are stable into adulthood. It has even been suggested that DNA methylation may in fact modulate the relationship between negative parenting behaviours and subsequent maladaptive psychosocial adjustment in later adolescence; however, these dynamics have yet to be examined with more comprehensive measures that are equipped to capture 'good' parenting or the granularity of early human experience. As such, we aim to investigate DNA methylation, childhood psychosocial and cognitive outcomes, and their relation to parenting quality. By using detailed and advanced measures, we hope to uncover the relationship between these three complex domains.

column36: Rythmes theta dans l'hippocampe ventral : roles dans le comportement emotionnel et modulation par la serotonine
column37: L'hippocampe (HP) peut etre divise en deux sous-regions. La region dorsale (HPd) est impliquee dans la memoire spatiale. La region ventrale (HPv) est impliquee dans l'anxiete, la memoire emotionnelle et les interactions sociales. Le rythme theta est une activite cerebrale de 6-12 Hz presente dans tout l'HP. On en connait beaucoup plus sur le rythme theta dans l'HPd que dans l'HPv. On sait que le rythme theta dans l'HPv varie selon l'anxiete, mais on ne sait toujours pas comment il est lie a la memoire sociale ou emotionnelle. Mon premier objectif est de caracteriser le rythme theta de l'HPv.Pour ce faire, je vais enregistrer le rythme theta dans l'HP de souris pendant plusieurs tests et analyser la variation des rythmes theta selon le comportement. Nous pensons que les proprietes du theta seront affectees seulement dans l'HPv. Les neurones serotoninergiques (5-HT) du raphe median (RM) jouent un role central dans l'anxiete et seraient en bonne position pour moduler le rythme theta dans l'HPv. Le second objectif est d'etablir le role de la 5-HT dans la modulation des rythmes theta dans l'HPv en lien avec le comportement anxieux. Pour l'objectif 2, je vais utiliser l'optogenetique, qui permet d'activer les neurones grace a la lumiere. Les neurones 5-HT MR-HPv seront actives dans un test d'anxiete, et l'effet sur les rythmes theta dans l'HPv et l'HPd sera evalue. Nous pensons que le rythme theta dans l'HPv mais pas dans l'HPd sera modifie et que la variation des rythme theta seront predictifs du degre d'anxiete. Tous les anxiolytiques affectent le rythme theta chez l'humain, au contraire des antipsychotiques ou des sedatifs. Une meilleure comprehension de la regulation du rythme theta est essentielle pour comprendre les mecanismes neurobiologiques de l'anxiete.

column36: Exploring the perspectives of genetic counsellors, medical interpreters, and patients with limited English proficiency in genetic counselling sessions requiring interpretation services
column37: Genetic counsellors are responsible for explaining genetic information and counselling to their patients. Interpreters are often used during genetic counselling sessions with limited English proficiency (LEP) patients. The majority of time during these sessions is spent translating between parties. Due to the time constraints, patient's psychosocial concerns are often neglected. Also, less detailed information is delivered. It is not known whether interpreters are effective in providing genetic information to LEP patients. There is also a lack of information about whether LEP patients feel empowered to make informed decisions. There are no studies that look at LEP patient's perspectives on genetic counselling appointments that use interpreters. Our study aims to look at the perspectives of genetic counsellors, interpreters, and LEP patients. We also aim to obtain suggestions from the LEP patient population that can be implemented to help provide equitable and optimal care. To explore this, we will use a mixed-methods approach. Participants will complete a survey focusing on genetic terminology translation, empowerment, and informed consent. Participants will then be interviewed about their genetic counselling experience. The interviews will be transcribed, and common themes will be identified. Our study will provide insight into patients' level of empowerment following their genetic counselling session. This research will guide recommendations on how to improve the genetic counselling experience for the LEP patient population.

column36: How are Canadians exposed to Extended-Spectrum Beta-Lactamase-Producing Enterobacteriaceae?
column37: This project aims to describe the relative contribution of the animal food production pathway to other pathways that can expose Canadians to resistant bacteria, in particular extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacteriaceae (ESBL-PE). It is part of, and informed by, a larger initiative coordinated by Public Health Agency of Canada called 'Integrated Assessment Modelling of Antimicrobial Resistance' (iAM.AMR), which was created to quantify exposure of Canadians to antimicrobial-resistant bacteria from select agri-food production systems. To determine the relative contribution of the animal food production pathway to the overall human exposure of ESBL-PE, this project will apply a One Health approach to summarize the potential transmission pathways of ESBL-producing bacteria. The resulting transmission map will address the complexity of how ESBL-PE affect and are affected by different reservoirs and hosts. It will also highlight and improve understanding of the impact of these pathogens on human, animal, and environmental health. This project also examines the burden of ESBL-PE on human health by characterizing the routes of exposure for humans. A scoping review is being performed to identify factors that influence the risk of being colonized or infected with an ESBL-PE. Data about the factors identified in the scoping review will be extracted and modeled using the iAM.AMR framework to estimate ESBL-PE exposures from different sources (human, animal, or environment). By improving our understanding of avenues for exposure and subsequent risks for colonization or infection with resistant bacteria, this project will contribute to prioritization and development of interventions and guidelines that aim to reduce the impact of antimicrobial resistance on Canadians.
