column36: The role of the ste20-like kinase (SLK) in Her2-driven breast cancers
column37: The HER2-positive breast cancer subtype accounts for approximately 25% of all breast cancer and is generally associated with a poor prognosis. Although the development of targeted therapeutics over the past 20 years has improved the prognosis, resistance to these therapeutics remains a significant concern which is driving a need for novel therapeutics. Our lab has been studying the Ste20-like kinase (SLK) for the past 20 years. We have shown that SLK is activated downstream of HER2 through multiple signaling pathways. Consequently, HER2-positive patients tend to exhibit an upregulation in SLK expression correlated with reduced overall survival. This is believed to be in part by SLK's role in promoting cell migration and proliferation. Surprisingly, previous work in our lab showed that loss of SLK in a mouse model of HER2-positive breast cancer significantly accelerated tumor onset and decreased overall survival. This was attributed to the activation of Sox10, a marker of the triple-negative breast cancer subtype. Our results suggest that SLK deletion causes reprogramming of HER2-positive tumors into triple-negative breast cancer. Interestingly, SLK has been shown to regulate cellular functions in a kinase activity-independent manner. It is possible that the loss of SLK scaffolding in SLK-deficient mice activates a pathway which upregulates Sox10 expression. We will test this by assessing the scaffolding function of SLK in tumor progression and Sox10 gene induction. Using CRISPR/Cas technology we have generated mice expressing kinase-inactive SLK. We will cross these mice with HER2-positive breast cancer model mice to assess tumor formation and progression, as well as characterize endpoint tumors. Results will be compared to both wild type and SLK-deficient mice.

column36: Cartographie des croyances complotistes et de la detresse psychologique durant la pandemie de COVID-19 au Canada
column37: La pandemie de COVID-19 et les consignes sanitaires qui visent a limiter sa transmission affectent la sante mentale et le bien- etre des Canadiens. L'evolution des connaissances scientifiques et l'ajustement frequent des recommandations de sante publique contribuent au climat d'incertitude et de perte de controle individuel qui favorise la propagation de la desinformation et des croyances erronees sur la maladie. L'objectif general du projet sera de preciser l'interrelation complexe entre les croyances complotistes et la detresse psychologique, et de cerner leurs determinants sociaux sous-jacents. Le projet s'inscrit dans l'etude pancanadienne COHESION, menee sur 10 000 individus et familles, qui collecte des donnees en temps reel, via une application mobile telechargeable, sur les symptomes anxiodepressifs, les interactions sociales, la mobilite, les espaces d'activites, les conditions de vie et les attitudes par rapport a la pandemie de COVID-19 dans le but de comprendre comment celle-ci affecte la sante et les inegalites sociales de sante. Un questionnaire initial et des questionnaires de suivis mensuels permettront de decrire les variations spatiotemporelles des indicateurs de detresse psychologique et de croyances erronees liees a la pandemie, et d'analyser l'effet de causes distales (ex. : capital social, environnement social du quartier) sur leur interrelation. La mise en evidence de determinants sociaux et d'une cartographie commune a la sante mentale et aux croyances complotistes pourraient orienter les efforts actuels et a venir des autorites de sante publique dans leur travail de proximite aupres des communautes plus reticentes a suivre les consignes sanitaires, surtout a l'approche d'une campagne de vaccination massive contre la COVID-19.

column36: Analyzing Performance of Braced vs Non-Braced Soccer Players after Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction
column37: Soccer players who suffer an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury rarely wear a protective knee brace when returning to sport, even when the Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA) rules allow the use of protective braces to be worn if padding is covering the brace. And players who return from ACL reconstruction (ACLR) surgery are at a higher risk of suffering another ACL injury. If soccer players appear to be at an increased risk of injury and protective knee braces can be worn, then why do players not wear a brace? One reason for players not wearing a knee brace may be because wearing a brace may impair the players potential performance. Therefore, the purpose of this study aims to identify if soccer specific performance-related differences exist between soccer players who have undergone ACLR and wear a knee brace, compared to soccer players who have undergone ACLR and do not wear a knee brace, compared to a healthy population. Soccer performance will be measured via kicking force by having participant's kick a soccer ball at a net with their injured leg, agility test performance will be measured by how fast participants can complete the test, and electromyography (EMG) will be recorded for both the kicking and agility test. The EMG readings will be measuring the quadriceps muscle group and the hamstring muscle group. Participants' performance level may vary ranging from recreational to professional. The results from this study can be applied to real-world scenarios, to see if performance-related differences exist by wearing a protective knee brace and if players can wear a knee brace without a decrease in performance.

column36: Effects of Functional Resistance Training Programs on Lung Cancer Symptomatology
column37: The proposed study is a 12-week, single group pilot-trial in individuals with lung cancer. Data will be collected at two, one-hour in-person study visits at baseline and 12-weeks at the Clinical Exercise Physiology Lab at the University of British Columbia. After baseline testing, participants will attend a 45-minute exercise class twice per week via a video-conferencing system that is approved for use by BC Cancer, led by a cancer and exercise specialist. The exercise prescription will consist of functional movements activating the large upper and lower body muscle groups. At the first study visit, participants will be familiarized with the video application and exercise prescription. The sample will consist of 30 individuals undergoing systemic treatment for stage III-IV small or non-small cell lung cancer. Dr. Laskin will provide leadership with recruitment and eligibility, which will centre on physician referral by medical oncologists at BC Cancer Vancouver. Patient adherence will be calculated as the ratio of training sessions completed out of the total possible sessions. Safety will be determined by no serious adverse events related to the intervention. Accrual will be represented as the number of participants recruited in two, 4-week periods. Physical function, lower-body strength, range of motion, power and functional capacity will be assessed using the Short Physical Performance Battery, chair stand time, sit and reach and back scratch tests of The Senior Fitness Test, Timed-Up-And-Go, and 6-minute walk tests, respectively. Fatigue and QOL will be measured by the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue and Lung surveys, respectively. Depressive Symptoms will be assessed by the Centre for Epidemiological Studies Depression survey.

column36: Elucidating genotype-phenotype relationships in novel kidney disease genes
column37: Chronic kidney disease affects approximately one in ten Canadians and puts an enormous strain on the public health care system. Genetic causes of chronic kidney disease account for up to 30% of cases in children and about 10% of cases in adults. Several kidney disease genes have been identified, but many are still unknown. Genetic kidney disease in children is particularly devastating, often presenting with an unremitting course towards complete loss of kidney function. The treatment options are hemodialysis, to filter toxins out of the blood, or kidney transplantation. While kidney transplants are the better choice, with improved survival, there are not enough donor kidneys available. In 2017, more than 25,000 Canadians required treatment with dialysis, while more than 200 patients died while waiting for an organ transplant. This highlights the urgent need to identify patients at risk of chronic kidney disease and to develop new therapies that prevent progression to complete renal failure. My proposed research project at the McGill University Health Centre aims to improve the diagnosis of genetic kidney disease and to improve the understanding of these disease mechanisms. Our goal is to elucidate the role of a newly identified kidney-disease gene using patient-derived cells and zebrafish animal models. These models can then be used to screen for new drug therapies. We expect this work to lay a foundation for the development of new treatment options for hereditary forms of kidney disease in children, for which currently no treatment exists.

column36: The role of intestinal stromal myofibroblasts in inflammation and infection
column37: Stromal cells of the intestinal connective tissue were previously overlooked as passive, structural cells. However, a growing body of evidence indicates that intestinal stromal cells play active roles in maintaining homeostasis by regulating the intestinal stem cell niche and the epithelial barrier through secretory pathways. In response to mucosal pathogens, studies have suggested that stromal cells alter their secretion of soluble mediators to drive epithelial regeneration. In the context of our project, we are interested in Rspo2 production related to the Wnt signaling pathway and Prostaglandin-2 signaling pathways, both recently shown to originate from intestinal stromal cells and communicate with neighboring intestinal epithelial cells. Our goal is to further understand the upstream signaling events triggering the production of these secreted factors and evaluate the genetic changes that they have on intestinal epithelial cells. By generating a greater understanding of the molecular pathways underlying intestinal regeneration, these studies will set the stage for developing new therapeutics that mimic the tissue-regenerative effects against invasive pathogens.

column36: 3D Printed Scaffolds for Stabilization and Local Therapeutic Delivery in Bone Metastases
column37: There has been a recent rise in cancer occurrence and increase in the risk of metastatic cancer, which is the spreading of cancer in the body from a primary source. Bone is the third most common site for metastases, with breast and prostate tumors often the primary source. Bone metastases can cause pain, instability and fractures. The current gold standard of treatment involves removing large sections of the bone that have been affected by the cancer. One limitation of surgical resection is that very small amounts of residual tumor are often left behind. With patients' survival time increasing, they are faced with high risk of recurrence and re-operation. Bone tumor resections often cause critical size defects which cannot self-repair and require additional support for stabilization and bone regeneration. Our team has been developing devices that can both support bone formation and locally deliver drugs that will eliminate residual tumor cells. 3D printing is an ideal method for this as it is cost-effective and produces unique, patient-specific geometries. We aim to generate composite scaffolds from two polymer types: a stiff one that contains mineral which supports bone repair, and a sponge-like polymer that can be loaded with therapeutics for local delivery. We aim to 1) test the scaffolds' mechanical integrity, 2) test the scaffolds' ability to deliver chemotherapeutics to breast and prostate cancer cells in vitro and 3) test the scaffolds in a rat model of bone metastasis where we will monitor bone repair, mechanical stability and inhibition of cancer recurrence following resection. Based on our preliminary work, we expect that the composite scaffolds will drive bone regeneration and successfully deliver sufficient chemotherapeutics to eradicate the residual cancer.

column36: Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor Activation by Cannabinoids Protects Against Lung Inflammation
column37: The Canadian Government fully legalized cannabis in 2018. Cannabis consumption is primarily through inhalation of cannabis smoke which allows cannabinoids and other smoke components to enter the body through the lungs. Despite legalization there is much uncertainty regarding the short- and long-term impacts of cannabis. Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) and cannabidiol (CBD) are the most well-known cannabinoids found in cannabis. Aside from psychoactive effects, THC has been shown to decrease airway inflammation in mice. CBD is the most abundant non-psychoactive cannabinoid found in cannabis and also possesses anti-inflammatory properties. Vaporization, which heats the dried plant without igniting it, may be a therapeutic means to deliver cannabinoids in the absence of the carcinogens found in smoke. Cannabinoids are known to bind to cannabinoid receptors CB1 and CB2 as well as the GPCR55. However, our data show that there is little expression of these receptors in lung epithelial cells. Cannabinoids may exert their beneficial properties via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR), which is always expressed in lung epithelial and endothelial cells. As THC and CBD increase AhR activity, the objectives of my research are to determine the effects of these select cannabinoids as well as cannabis smoke on AhR function, and to furthermore assess the capacity of cannabinoids in attenuating the lung inflammation. I hypothesize that AhR activation by cannabinoids protects against lung inflammation associated with the damage in chronic lung diseases. This project will determine the therapeutic potential of cannabis in maintaining respiratory health by providing an improved understanding of the effects of cannabis on inflammation.

column36: La rigidite aortique et la fonction vasculaire cerebrale chez les patients insuffisants renaux chroniques
column37: L'insuffisance renale chronique (IRC) affecte pres de 4 millions de canadiens et est caracterisee par une diminution de la capacite des reins a filtrer les dechets metaboliques. L'ensemble des desordres metaboliques associes a l'IRC augmente le risque de complications cardiovasculaires. De plus, on observe chez les patients IRC un declin cognitif accelere qui s'accentue avec la severite de la dysfonction renale. Bien que les mecanismes sous-jacents demeurent meconnus, la rigidite aortique semble impliquee. En IRC, la rigidite aortique est accrue et augmente la pulsatilite de la pression qui se propage vers la microcirculation des organes cibles tels que le cerveau. Certaines etudes suggerent d'autant plus que la rigidite arterielle, au niveau cerebral, pourrait nuire a la regulation du debit sanguin cerebral. En temps normal, plusieurs mecanismes permettent la regulation du debit sanguin cerebral et protegent le cerveau des dommages secondaires a l'hyperperfusion ou l'hypoperfusion. Les principaux sont la reactivite vasculaire cerebrale au dioxyde de carbone et l'autoregulation cerebrale dynamique. Ces mecanismes permettent de moduler le debit sanguin cerebral en reponse aux changements de pression partielle de dioxyde de carbone et de la pression arterielle, respectivement, et pourraient etre alteres en IRC. C'est pourquoi nous proposons de caracteriser les mecanismes de regulation du debit sanguin cerebral dans une population d'IRC et d'evaluer l'impact de perte de fonction renale et de la rigidite aortique sur ces mecanismes.

column36: Roles des proteines SNX1 et SNX2 dans le routage intracellulaire du recepteur MET dans les cellules du cancer colorectal resistantes a l'apoptose.
column37: Deux caracteristiques principales de la tumorigenese et du developpement des metastases sont le besoin d'une stimulation constante de la croissance cellulaire, souvent via un recepteur tyrosine kinase (RTK), et la resistance a l'apoptose causee par les caspases. Cette resistance implique des mecanismes en amont des caspases executrices, les peptidases provoquant la mort cellulaire par apoptose, mais en aval des caspases initiatrices, emp echant la cellule de mourir. Ainsi, dans les cellules resistantes, le clivage des proteines par les caspases initiatrices peut se produire sans que la cellule ne meure. Notre equipe a identifie deux proteines, SNX1 et SNX2, impliquees dans le routage et la signalisation des RTK, plus particulierement celui du recepteur du facteur de croissance hepatocytaire (HGF) MET qui est implique dans la pathogenese du cancer colorectal (CCR). Nous proposons que le clivage par la caspase-8 initiatrice de certains substrats, dont SNX1 et SNX2, exacerbe le phenotype malin des cellules cancereuses resistante a l'apoptose. Consequemment, le projet d'Amelie consiste a : Objectif 1 - Valider le role de SNX1 et SNX2 dans le routage intracellulaire du recepteur MET a l'aide de lignees cellulaires HCT-116 du CCR KO pour une et ces deux proteines. Une serie d'essais dont la microscopie confocale et le suivi du recepteur dans les differentes voies endocytiques, et l'etude de la cinetique d'internalisation du recepteur seront utilises; Objectif 2 - Comprendre comment leur clivage de SNX1 et SNX2 et leurs fragments de clivage alterent le routage intracellulaire de MET a l'aide de techniques de microscopie confocale et d'ELISA. Ce projet permettra d'identifier SNX1 et SNX2 comme des joueurs cles de la biologie du recepteur MET dans le CCR.

column36: Effects of Previous Coronavirus Infections on the Immune Response to SARS-CoV-2 Infection
column37: COVID-19 is caused by SARS-CoV-2, which has infected over 56 million people globally since its emergence in late 2019, causing profound disruptions in our daily lives. It is a member of the coronavirus family, which also houses a group of viruses called HCoVs that are responsible for the common cold. The surface of a virus is unique like a fingerprint. The adaptive immune system designs antibodies that will specifically recognize and attach to patterns on a particular virus to fight the infection. This response is then saved into the immune system's memory so that the next time the fingerprint is seen, antibodies can be released nearly immediately. This response forms the basis of vaccinations. But what happens when a new virus' fingerprint is very similar to a previously encountered one's? This is often the case for the flu, where the vaccine changes almost yearly because the virus is constantly mutating. If a flu shot contains a similar enough fingerprint to a previously encountered virus, the individual develops a strengthened response to the earlier virus and no response and no protection against the one in the vaccine. This is known as the original antigenic sin (OAS) and describes how our immune system prefers to use immune memory whenever possible. We believe the severe symptoms seen in COVID-19 are a result of OAS generating an excess of antibodies directed against HCoVs rather than SARS-CoV-2 as they are very similar. Our study aims to use antibody tests to identify the antibodies generated throughout the course of SARS-CoV-2 infection to determine if OAS results in worse COVID-19 outcomes. Our findings will not only help identify those at highest risk for severe symptoms, but will also provide insight for COVID-19 vaccination strategies.

column36: DSM-5 Personality Domains in Treatment Seeking Bilingual Iranians: A Cross-Cultural Invariance Study
column37: Personality disorders (PDs) can disturb the affected individual, those around them, and even society at large. The Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.; DSM-5) considers PDs as long lasting maladaptive patterns of behaviour, cognition, and inner experience. Criterion B in its Section III is the descriptive diagnostic core and is composed of dimensional pathological personality traits organized in five main domains. These five domains are composed of 25 lower-order trait-facets. The assessment of these is operationalized using the Personality Inventory for DSM-5 (PID-5). The PID-5 has proved valid and reliable in a variety of countries but the PID-5 translated into Farsi is limited to only a few studies and lacks validity. Therefore, establishing cross-cultural validity for the Farsi version is crucial. The goal of the current cross-cultural invariance study is to investigate whether the lower order facet-traits can be extracted from the PID-5 Farsi version by administering both the Farsi and English versions to a bilingual Iranian clinical sample. The study will include 200 treatment seeking Iranian adults residing in Canada who are fluent in Farsi and English. Once English and Farsi fluency is confirmed using the Wide Range Achievement Test and bilingual Iranian researchers, participants will proceed to complete the English and Farsi versions of the PID-5 in a counterbalanced order. Exploratory factor analysis will be used to examine the emerging facet-trait structure of the Farsi PID-5. This study will assist clinicians in making diagnosis for Iranian Canadians and also establish validity for the Farsi PID-5. This study will also facilitate the study of cultural differences in personality psychopathology between Western countries and Iran.

column36: Role of CD13 in the context of breast cancer
column37: The presence and risk for breast cancer is implicated in a variety of factors. Specifically, oncogenes like Erbb2, Myc, and Ras, which are genes that have the potential to contribute to cancer development, can be mutated or overexpressed, promoting tumour formation. Tumours are generally groups of abnormal cells with distinct morphological and functional characteristics, including irregular shape and size, growth rate, and mobility. Although tumours are composed of various types of cells, one group of cells called epithelial cells organize themselves into complex structures without losing their characteristic cavity called the central lumen. This lumen is directly required for cells to orient themselves properly. A key determinant of epithelial polarity orientation is a transmembrane protein called Aminopeptidase N (CD13). In the presence of Ras oncogene, our lab previously discovered that in its absence, cells displayed inverted polarities, failing to form central lumens. When CD13 was reintroduced, cells were able to regain their correct polarity and re-enter the normal cell cycle, undergoing programmed cell death. Our aims in this study are to understand the role of CD13 in the presence of Erbb2 and Myc oncogenes to investigate its potential as a therapeutic target for breast cancer therapy.

column36: Optimization and characterization of expanded NKreg cells for therapy of chronic graft-versus-host disease
column37: Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplantation (HSCT) is a critical immune-based therapeutic option for patients with high-risk and relapsed blood cancers. However, HSCT is attributed to an increased risk of complications, the most severe being chronic graft-versus-host-disease (cGvHD), in which foreign donor immune cells attack the recipient's tissues. cGvHD occurs in 25% of pediatric and 60% of adult HSCT survivors. It is known to cause chronic organ damage and has a 10-25% mortality rate. My team has identified a cGvHD biomarker (a non-cytolytic CD56bright Natural Killer population (NKreg)) closely correlated with an inhibition of cGvHD. Further, the adoptive transfer of expanded cytolytic NK cells has shown to potentially decrease leukemia relapse with no increase in GvHD. Thus, we hypothesize that the adoptive transfer of expanded NKreg cells after HSCT represents a significant strategy to decrease cGvHD without increasing leukemia relapse. To address my hypothesis, I will first determine the functional characteristics of CD56bright non-cytolytic NKreg cells associated with successful and failed suppression of cGvHD. Second, I will optimize and operationalize the expansion of functional NKreg cells. Third, I will evaluate the effect of expanded NKreg cells on cGvHD effector and suppressor immune populations in in vitro and in vivo models. In completion of my proposed research, I expect to understand the characteristics of human CD56bright NKreg cells that associate with no development of cGvHD and establish an optimal expansion protocol. These approaches will provide a biological understanding for developing strategies to augment NKreg cells as an adoptive transfer therapy for cGvHD, significantly contributing to the goal of improving the safety and efficacy of HSCT.

column36: Discovery of potential new antibiotics in Canadian High Arctic bacteria
column37: Discovery of potential new antibiotics in Canadian High Arctic bacteria Eszter Farkas, Dr. Dao Nguyen, Dr. Samantha Gruenheid Due to the worldwide antibiotic resistance crisis, there has been an urgent call for the discovery and development of new antibiotics. Unfortunately, there has been a significant decrease in the discovery of new antibiotics in the past few decades. Many of the antibiotics used today were originally compounds produced by bacteria from the soil. This had led researchers to explore understudied environments such as the Arctic, an extreme environment which has a large diversity of bacteria. Furthermore, the uniqueness of the Arctic may cause bacteria to evolve differently than those in our local environments and therefore produce different compounds. The diversity of this region coupled with the unique environmental pressures of this region make it an untapped environment to search for bacteria that produce compounds with potentially new antibiotic activity. Our collaborators isolated bacteria from Arctic soil and identified bacterial isolates that display promising and novel antibacterial activity in preliminary studies. For this project, I will further characterize the antibacterial activity of these isolates against a number of human pathogens and identify the antibacterial compounds produced by the most promising bacterial isolates. Through this project, we aim to explore Arctic bacteria as a potential source of new antibacterial compounds for the discovery of new antibiotics.

column36: Magnetic resonance imaging with gadolinium-labeled porphysomes
column37: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has developed into one of the most powerful diagnostic tools in biomedicine. However, due to the relatively low sensitivity of MRI for tumor diagnosis, contrast agents (CAs) are used to improve the quality of MR images. Most common MRI CAs use gadolinium (Gd) ions due to its enhancing spatial resolution and brightening effects. Currently, most clinically approved Gd-incorporated CAs show limited efficiency, are non-targeting and are rapidly cleared from the blood. Incorporating Gd ions into nanoparticles has allowed for the ability to load up to hundreds of thousands of Gd ions per structure, modifying it to include tumor targeting, and enhance its multimodality. However, previously designed particles are either toxic, inorganic, or lack multifunctionality. Thus, a safer and more effective Gd-incorporated nanostructure is essential in order to translate such technology into the clinical stages. Porphysome nanovesicles, which were discovered within the Zheng lab, are fully organic and multimodal imaging CAs that can be tracked within the body and deliver drugs to diseased tissues. Recently, porphysome formulations in the lab have included the labelling of Gd, adding MR imaging potential onto the nanoparticles' multimodal imaging toolbox. To test the hypothesis on if porphysomes can act as MRI CAs, I propose to work with a variety of different formulated Gd-labelled porphysomes, testing their efficacy in pancreatic cancer cell and mouse models, with plans of further modifying them to enhance their targeting ability on a specific disease. With porphysomes being on the verge of entering its 1st-in-patient clinical trial, proving they can act as effective MRI CAs will also offer them high clinical translation potential.

column36: Investigating the contribution of methionine metabolism in the development of drug resistance by modulating chromatin landscapes
column37: Triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive form of breast cancer that has a poor prognosis due to the high incidence of resistance to chemotherapy drugs. Drug resistance acquired in cancer cells is partly related to changes in cell metabolism and in gene regulation. Certain chemical changes that take place in DNA in the nucleus of the cell are called epigenetic changes and control which genes are expressed or not. These epigenetic processes are modulated by the availability of certain nutrients in the cell, called metabolites. While the availability of some of these metabolites can induce epigenetic changes and thus influence gene expression, epigenetic changes can in turn also control the levels and use of metabolites. This inter-regulation allows the tumour to adapt and survive in the context of a new environment, such as that resulting from exposure to drugs. The main objective of our research is to understand how metabolic and epigenetic changes regulate each other in drug-resistant TNBC in order to identify new ways to re-sensitize TNBC cells to chemotherapy. We have developed TNBC cells that are resistant to paclitaxel, a standard treatment drug for patients with TNBC. We are interested in understanding the role of methionine, an essential nutrient in the diet, in drug resistance. This is because drug resistant TNBC cells use more methionine than drug sensitive cells. We aim to identify how changes in methionine use in drug-resistant TNBC cells impact the production and use of other metabolites in order to identify potential vulnerabilities in resistant cells. We will also assess how these changes in methionine use contribute to altering epigenetic modifications and what the impact is on gene expression in paclitaxel-resistant TNBC cells.

column36: Investigating novel peripheral blood biomarkers for disease activity and treatment response in multiple sclerosis
column37: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is an autoimmune disease of the central nervous system (CNS) and represents the most common neurological disorder among young adults. There is no blood test to follow disease activity. A biomarker is a biological indicator of disease activity. Because of the variable course of the disease and inconsistent response to treatments, the lack of readily measurable biomarkers is an obstacle to the early and correct treatment of people with MS. To address this clinical need, I used gene expression analysis to uncover differences between immune cells from MS patients and healthy controls. I hypothesize that the levels of proteins resulting from the expression of differently expressed genes can be indicative of relapses and/or response to treatment. To conduct my biomarker study, I will study seven potential biomarkers simultaneously on individual cells using a technique called flow cytometry. I will analyze immune cells from a bank of MS patient samples in the Prat lab. I will select samples from MS patients at different stages of the disease, with different disease activity, under different treatments, and at different timepoints in their disease course. Next, I will compare the levels of the potential biomarkers on different immune cell types in the conditions listed above. Finally, I will correlate the flow cytometry data with clinical and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. This may lead to the first MS blood biomarker for potential clinical use. Such a biomarker could allow physicians to predict patient disease course, but also to effectively determine treatment response and thus promote rapid adjustments to treatment regimes. This would undoubtedly promote better clinical care of people with MS and drastically improve their quality of life.

column36: Mechanisms of neural stem cell fate selection in the neonatal brain
column37: Injury to the skin, such as a cut, usually heals perfectly. In contrast, when the brain gets injured, we are often left with lifelong damage. Therefore, in order to improve quality of life, it is important to identify ways of promoting brain repair following damage. One such strategy looks to use specialized cells within the brain, called neural stem cells (NSCs), which are uniquely capable of producing nervous system cells (called interneurons and oligodendrocytes) throughout life. Because of this ability, we believe that we may ultimately be able to use these NSCs to instruct the brain to heal itself following injury. In order to do so, we need to gain a better understanding of NSCs and how they function. Though significant progress has been made in recent years, there is still much that we don't know about these cells, such as how they build the brain during development, and how they decide on what specific cell types to make within the newborn brain. My project seeks to shed light on these processes, with the goal of understanding how we may instruct NSCs to form oligodendrocytes or neurons following injury. To this end, I will first determine whether individual NSCs, in the newborn brain, are capable of giving rise to multiple different types of cells. Next, I will test whether NSCs can be convinced to generate one cell type instead of another by growing these cells in the presence of various factors. Finally, I will use a mixture of computational and biological techniques to gain insight into the mechanisms by which NSCs give rise to distinct cell types. Altogether, this research will allow us to better appreciate how NSCs function during development and throughout life, and may provide clues as to how we can recruit these cells to promote brain regeneration.

column36: Exploring the relationship of COVID-19 with stigma and mental health among community-based outreach workers in the Philippines
column37: Non-governmental organizations (NGOs) are critical to the COVID-19 response in low- and middle-income countries as they continue to deliver services to low-resource communities. In the context of the COVID-19 pandemic, health workers have been discriminated against due to ongoing exposure to the virus, with NGOs identifying comparable experiences among staff members engaged in outreach work. As a result, there is a need to understand the association between COVID-19 diagnoses, stigma, and mental health among NGO staff. This research will be conducted in partnership with International Care Ministries (ICM), a NGO delivering poverty alleviation interventions in the Philippines. The aim of this research is to investigate the association of mental health outcomes and perceived stigma with COVID-19 test results among ICM outreach staff (e.g. health educators, social workers) in the Philippines. Data will be collected from n=350 ICM staff members. COVID-19 test results will be extracted from ICM occupational reports prepared from October 2020 to April 2021. In May 2021, mental health and perceived stigma will be measured through the Kessler-10 Psychological Distress Scale (K-10) and Perceived Stigma Scale, respectively. Information on sociodemographic and occupational factors will also be collected. Multiple linear regression will be used to analyze the associations between COVID-19 test results with the K-10 and Perceived Stigma Scale scores. Analyses will be controlled for sociodemographic factors, occupational responsibilities, and geographic location. This research can inform the creation of mental health resources for frontline healthcare and social service workers that operate outside of the formal health care system in low-resource settings.

column36: Investigating the Structural Basis for HflX Mediated Antibiotic Resistance
column37: Antibiotic resistance in pathogens is an increasing problem. It is estimated that by 2050, more people will die from antibiotic resistance related diseases than from cancer. It is imperative that new antibiotic targets be identified and/or new antibiotics developed. The protein HflX is found in all pathogenic bacteria. HflX aids in helping cells create proteins from amino acids. The cellular biological machine responsible for making proteins is called the ribosome. When cells are exposed to stressful conditions, the ribosome can stall and protein production will halt. HflX is able to restart protein synthesis by splitting the 70S ribosome. Recently, HflX in the bacteria Listeria monocytogenes was shown to provide the cell with resistance to lincosamide and macrolide antibiotics. This function has been linked with HflXr's ability to split the 70S ribosome. As this was a new function not previously described for HflX, the researchers named it HflX resistance (HflXr). The differences between HflX and HflXr that give rise to antibiotic resistance is not obvious. The unique amino acid sequences found in HflXr are likely the source of the antibiotic resistance. To this end, the objective of this research project will be to elucidate the biochemical mechanism by which HflXr can convey antibiotic resistance and to further characterize the overall mechanism by which HflX splits the 70S ribosome. This will be done via ribosome dissociation experiments, complementation assays, and structural studies utilizing cryo-electron microscopy. Unveiling the mechanism by which HflX conveys antibiotic resistance will be important for the development of antibiotics that counteract either HflX itself or the process that it is facilitating (rescuing stalled ribosomes).

column36: Long term outcomes and health care utilization following de novo cardioverter-defibrillator implantation for primary prevention: 10-year follow-up from the Ontario ICD database
column37: Sudden cardiac death is a leading cause of mortality in developed countries. Landmark trials have shown that implantable cardioverter-defibrillators (ICDs) reduce all-cause mortality in patients known arrhythmia for secondary prevention, as well as asymptomatic patients with both ischemic and non-ischemic cardiomyopathy for primary prevention. However, ICD patients in the ""real world"" are often older with a greater burden of comorbidities than those from randomized controlled trials, placing them at higher risk of procedure complications, prolonged hospitalizations, and increased health care costs. Since longevity of ICD devices range from 5 to 10 years, many patients will eventually require replacement procedures. There is a paucity of high-quality evidence on the experiences with long-term ICD therapy in the ""real-world"". To our knowledge this project will be the first to use population-level health administrative data housed within the Ontario ICD database to describe predictors of mortality, ICD replacement, and health care utilization in a 10 year follow-up of adult patients who received de novo ICD therapy for primary prevention in Ontario between February 2007 and February 2011. This database is uniquely equipped for broadly inclusive data collection due to Ontario's single-payer health care system, including variables such as patient factors (socioeconomical status, age, sex), device factors (device type, number of leads), and operator factors (surgeon vs. non-surgeon, physician implantation volume). Identification of modifiable patient and system factors leading to health inequity and increased healthcare utilization will ultimately drive new health policies and guidelines towards improving the care of patients with ICD therapy in Canada.

column36: Role of LINC01081 and LINC01082 in alveolar capillary dysplasia with misalignment of pulmonary veins
column37: Alveolar capillary dysplasia with misalignment of pulmonary veins (ACD/MPV) is a rare and lethal congenital disease in which newborns die from respiratory distress due to impaired lung development. Near 40% of patients carry mutations in FOXF1, a transcription factor regulating the production of biomolecules for cell growth, proliferation and differentiation, hence master regulator of lung development. ACD/MPV patients without FOXF1 mutations have instead focal chromosomal deletions upstream the FOXF1 gene. This non-coding genomic region with three longs non-coding RNAs (lncRNA), might interact with FOXF1. Our laboratory previously showed that in mice, the loss of one of these lncRNAs, Fendrr, is perinatal lethal due to lung developmental defects reminiscent of ACD/MPV. It is unclear if the two other lung expressed lncRNAs, LINC01081 and LINC01082, play a role in lung cells and contribute to ACD/MPV. We hypothesize that they are vital for lung cells' proper functioning and contribute to ACD/MPV by regulating FOXF1 or its downstream effectors. To test this hypothesis, we aim to identify the impact of loss of LINC01081 and LINC01082 on FOXF1 and global gene expression in human lung fibroblasts and also their cellular role in regulating lung fibroblast behaviour. We will use various tools to eliminate these lncRNAs and assess its impact on the expression of FOXF1 and other genes. Cellular assays will be done to determine if their loss affects proliferation, cell death or migration of human lung fibroblasts. Hence, these experiments will provide major insights into the cellular and molecular roles of two lncRNAs associated with ACD/MPV and will support further in vivo and molecular studies. Thus, this may help develop novel and precise diagnostic tools for ACD/MPV.

column36: Targeting drug tolerant persisters in colorectal cancer via anti-apoptosis inhibition
column37: Targeting chemotherapy resistant cells in colorectal cancer Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third highest cause of cancer-related deaths in North America, and chemotherapy resistance presents a major challenge to successful therapy. In some cases, tumour cells enter a slow-growth state to escape chemotherapy and resume rapid growth once chemotherapy is stopped. These cells are known as drug tolerant persisters (DTPs) and are emerging as key players in mediating chemotherapy resistance. Our previous work showed that these DTPs were maintained by autophagy, a process through which cells recycle damaged cellular components for survival. Inhibition of autophagy using a small molecule inhibitors modestly increased cell death (apoptosis) of DTPs. To identify additional methods by which DTPs survive chemotherapy, we conducted an unbiased drug screen which indicated that DTPs increase anti-apoptosis proteins to prevent cell death, which I confirmed experimentally. We hypothesize that combining inhibitors of autophagy with inhibitors of anti-apoptosis proteins will significantly enhance tumour cell death. To do this, I will treat patient derived CRC cell cultures with anti-apoptosis inhibitors (Venetoclax, Navitoclax, or AMG-176) to determine whether these drugs induce tumour cell death. These drugs will then be combined with an autophagy inhibitor to see if there is increased cell death. If so, this treatment regimen will be tested in CRC mouse models. This project will contribute to a better understanding of DTPs in chemoresistance and uncover new mechanisms to target DTPs. Using Venetoclax for CRC treatment is very promising as it is already approved by the FDA, offering safe and rapid introduction of a new treatment regimen to improve CRC patient outcomes.

column36: Trafficking and folding of the hERG ion channel: implications for long QT syndrome type 2
column37: Cardiovascular disease is the number one cause of death worldwide. Dysfunction of the hERG/Kv11.1 ion channel is responsible for long QT syndrome type 2 (LQT2), which increases the risk of arrhythmia and cardiac arrest and is present in 1/2500 Caucasians. LQT2 patients have a single mutant copy of the gene, with mutations being linked to misfolding of the protein. A hERG channel consists of 4 copies of protein, and each can be either of two isoforms: hERG-1a is full length protein, while hERG-1b is missing the amino terminal domain. Since 1a can form functional channels alone while 1b cannot, most past research has focused only on 1a. However, channels with both 1a and 1b have different physiological properties. Hence, the molecular mechanisms behind LQT2 remain poorly characterized. We propose 2 mechanisms for LQT2: 1) Dominant negative (DN):mutant subunits associate with wild-type (WT) ones, making a non-functional channel. 2) Haploinsufficient (HI): mutant subunits do not associate with WT, meaning all surface channels are functional, but there are approximately half as many. Our preliminary research indicates that disease mutants lie on a spectrum between DN and HI. Using a model co-expression (1a/1b) system, we aim to determine the DN or HI mechanisms of LQT2-causing mutations, and correlate them to the molecular structure of hERG. We constructed mutant and normal genes with different tags so we can observe their interaction and localization. The results will be validated in human cardiomyocytes gene-edited with the mutations. With a better understanding of the folding and trafficking of hERG channels, our research will help predict the severity of disease for patients with known and novel LQT2 mutations and allow for the development of targeted treatments.

column36: Is Vascular Health in Cancer Survivors Improved Following 12-Weeks of Individualized Exercise Training?
column37: Compared to the rest of Canada, Nova Scotia has higher rates of new cancer diagnoses and cancer-related deaths. People with cancer have poor artery health, which leads to heart disease. Cancer patients have better upper-limb artery health following intense, supervised aerobic exercise programs. We do not know if less intense, community-based exercise programs can help people with cancer improve upper-limb artery health. We also do not know if such programs enhance lower-limb artery health, which may benefit more from commonly used walking and cycling exercises. Lower-limb arteries are also more likely to develop disease. The aim of this project is to find out if our 12-week community-based Activating Cancer Communities through an Exercise Strategy for Survivors (ACCESS) program improves upper- and lower-limb artery health in breast and prostate cancer patients. The 2 day/week supervised, and tailored ACCESS program uses both aerobic- and whole-body weight-based exercises. Artery health in the upper arm and lower leg will be measured using an ultrasound machine. Our test of artery health involves measuring how much larger an artery gets after blood flow to the hand or foot has been briefly stopped using a pressure cuff. Once the pressure cuff is released, artery blood flow increases, which causes the arteries to get bigger. The bigger the arteries get, the healthier they are. If the ACCESS program improves artery health then we can be more confident that it will help decrease the risk of getting heart disease. But, if it does not improve artery health, we can try to make changes that will make it better. These results can also help to inform the design and evaluation of other community-based cancer exercise programs in Canada.

column36: Le vecu des parents suivant un diagnostic de craniosynostose chez leur enfant.
column37: La craniosynostose est une maladie generalement diagnostiquee des la naissance qui touche un enfant sur 2 500. Le traitement habituel implique une craniectomie dans les premiers mois de vie de l'enfant. Les parents d'un enfant ayant recu un diagnostic de craniosynostose font face a une multitude d'evenements stressants et le moment entre l'annonce du diagnostic et la chirurgie est une periode de grande vulnerabilite vis-a-vis la detresse psychologique. Dans le but de mieux accompagner les parents durant cette periode, nous devons d'abord mieux comprendre les facteurs influencant le stress vecu et identifier les defis et les besoins selon leur perspective. Cent parents quebecois dont l'enfant a recu un diagnostic de craniosynostose dans les cinq dernieres annees repondront a des questionnaires en ligne. Ceux-ci permettront d'evaluer le stress parental (Parental Stress Index), l'impact de la condition de l'enfant sur leur vie personnelle, professionnelle, familiale et sociale (Parental Quality of Life) ainsi que leurs perceptions des besoins rencontres durant le processus de prise en charge. Les repondants seront ensuite invites a participer a une entrevue semi-dirigee a l'aide du Reaction to Diagnostic Interview afin d'echanger plus en details sur leur experience et leur adaptation a la condition de leur enfant. Les donnees recueillies permettront de mieux guider les equipes multidisciplinaires dans l'accompagnement des familles touchees par la craniosynostose.

column36: Effect of cannabidiol on sleep, seizure activity and memory in mouse models of GRIN1 disorder
column37: GRIN disorders are neurodevelopmental disorders caused by mutation to one of the GRIN genes. These genes carry the genetic information for NMDA receptors; neurotransmitter receptors that are critical for learning and memory. Children who have GRIN disorders present with varying degrees of intellectual disability, epilepsy, motor dysfunction and disordered sleep patterns. Many of these children have limited impairments, while others are unable to communicate and require assistance with basic tasks. Recent advances in genetic testing have led to the identification of the specific mutations carried by patients, however, there is little information known regarding how each mutation effects NMDA receptor function and ultimately contributes to the level of impairment in each individual. Characterizing the molecular and behavioral effects of these GRIN mutations would allow for the development of improved treatments specific to the mutation carried by the patient. To do this, we will utilize mouse models harboring the precise GRIN mutations of individual patients in order to characterize the molecular dysfunction and the resulting behavioral phenotype of each mutation. In addition, we will test the ability of cannabidiol, a constituent of marijuana known for its anti-convulsive and sleep altering qualities, to improve the phenotypes of these mice. In Specific Aim 1, we study NMDA receptor biochemistry and function in animal models. In Specific Aim 2, we assess the behavioral phenotypes of the mice in the domains of sleep, seizure activity and memory and the ability of cannabidiol to improve these phenotypes.

column36: The risk of acute kidney injury with fluoroquinolone use: describing exposure time trends to select the best study design and yield a valid estimate
column37: Antibiotics are an important type of medication used to treat bacterial infections. Fluoroquinolones (FQs) are one type of antibiotic that is commonly used for respiratory and urinary tract infections. Although FQs are highly effective for treating infections, there are concerns that they may increase the risk of acute kidney injury (AKI). AKI is associated with a decrease in kidney function, and an increased risk of medical complications and death. Although decreased kidney function after treatment with FQs has been seen in individual patients, the association has not been confirmed by studies observing large groups of people. The question of whether FQs increase AKI risk remains. We will examine the association between FQs and AKI by studying older adults exposed to FQs in Ontario. We will report results overall and for men and women separately. We will also consider the impact of different study design methods to answer our research question. FQs are one of the most commonly prescribed antibiotics among older adults in Ontario, and seniors are an age group at high risk for AKI. Thus, our results will have an important impact on prescribing decisions.

column36: Unraveling targetable protease networks in tumour and stroma subtypes of pancreatic cancer
column37: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is the most common form of pancreatic cancer. One major characteristic of PDAC is the stroma, or the tumour microenvironment. Recent studies identified subtypes based on the total RNA present in the tumours. Here, specific grouped genes in tumour and stroma cells identified two epithelial subtypes: the 'basal-like' and 'classical', and two stroma subtypes: 'mature/normal' and 'immature/activated'. The differing impact on disease progression may be due to difference in communication. The availability of these molecules depends on various factors, including the level of gene expression and processing by a protein called a protease. Their role in breaking down their molecular targets highlights the importance of proteases in regulating cell-to-cell communication. My project aims to investigate the differential expression of proteases at the subtype level. Using various datasets to quantify different levels of gene expression, first, I will define a shortlist of proteases with clear prognostic impact using computational means. This will be validated in tissues by quantifying protease expression. Our lab has created a workflow that allows semi-automated quantification of the level of staining in an image, and interrogation and visualization of our results. Second, experimental models will be used to address which of the candidate proteases are potential therapeutic targets; these models include growing tumour and stroma cells together and using patient-derived 3D culture systems. Identifying the proteases that differ between subtypes can bring to light new therapies for PDAC. Furthermore, my computational analysis will create a protease-resource for other studies to utilize and potentially find more candidates for future therapies.

column36: Understanding the Role of Uterine Natural Killer Immune Cells in Cannabis-Induced Pregnancy Complications
column37: In 2017 alone, nearly 2000 pregnant women in Ontario self-reported using cannabis during their pregnancy. However, prenatal cannabis use has likely increased following the 2018 Canadian legalization of cannabis, as studies in California found that cannabis use during pregnancy doubled following legalization. Reportedly, women using cannabis while pregnant have drastically increased occurrences of pregnancy complications, such as a 50% increased risk of stillbirth. However, little is known about how cannabis causes these complications. For a successful pregnancy, the uterus must create a favourable environment that supports fetal growth. This process is largely modulated by the immune system, particularly uterine Natural Killer (uNK) cells, which reside in the maternal tissue surrounding the fetus. These uNK cells are extensively involved in adapting the uterine environment to support pregnancy and their dysfunction underpins complications like recurrent pregnancy loss. Despite the crucial role of uNK cells for a successful pregnancy, no work has been done to understand how cannabis impacts their function. This project aims to investigate how cannabis affects the function of uNK cells during pregnancy by examining changes in uNK cell function following exposure to cannabis as well as how cannabis-induced uNK cell dysfunction results in pregnancy complications in a mouse model. The information gained from this work will provide a clear explanation of how cannabis is causing drastically increased occurrences of pregnancy complications. As prenatal cannabis use is rising rapidly, such information is urgently needed to motivate public health efforts to reduce prenatal cannabis use and inform women on the danger of using cannabis while pregnant.

column36: Approfondissement de la dependance alimentaire et ses impacts sur l'evolution du trouble d'acces hyperphagique
column37: De recentes etudes suggerent l'existence de similarites comportementales et neurobiologiques entre la surconsommation alimentaire liee a l'obesite et la dependance aux substances psychoactives. Plusieurs auteurs proposent de caracteriser la relation excessive, voire m eme compulsive, que certaines personnes developpent a l'egard de la nourriture comme une dependance alimentaire (DA). Les individus souffrants de DA rapporteraient davantage de difficultes psychologiques et des comportements alimentaires dysfonctionnels comme d'intenses envies alimentaires (cravings), et ce, malgre la connaissance des consequences sociales et physiques associees. En depit de la severite du profil clinique caracterisant la DA, peu d'etude a ce jour permettent de distinguer la DA d'autres troubles des conduites alimentaires (TCA) reconnus, notamment le trouble d'acces hyperphagique (TAH). Or, de plus amples connaissances sur la nature de la relation entre la DA et le TAH permettraient de mieux comprendre la contribution des symptomes de la DA sur l'evolution de ces troubles. Par exemple, est-ce que la DA est associee a une plus grande detresse psychologique ou une prise de poids plus rapide? Le present projet vise ainsi a approfondir la comprehension actuelle de la DA, afin de documenter et mieux comprendre ses impacts sur l'evolution du TAH et de l'obesite. Cette etude pourrait permettre de repousser les connaissances actuelles sur le traitement des TCA, de sorte a offrir le service le plus adapte en fonction des differents profils cliniques. Des recommandations en matiere de prevention pour les professionnels de la sante pourraient egalement favoriser une meilleure prise en charge des individus souffrants de TAH et d'obesite.

column36: Two Spirit peoples' experiences accessing and receiving care in community pharmacies
column37: Two Spirit people (a term used by Indigenous Peoples to encompass diverse gender and sexual identities) face unique challenges in accessing and receiving healthcare in Canada. Health services, including community pharmacy services, are built on hetero- and cis-normative models that impede appropriate care for Two Spirit peoples. This project aims to gain knowledge about the experiences of Two Spirit peoples in accessing and receiving care in community pharmacy settings in Canada. To address the lack of published information on this topic, Two Spirit individuals will be asked to share their experiences and knowledge in a sharing circle (virtually or in person depending on COVID-19 restrictions). In the same sharing circle, community pharmacists will be asked to share the extent and limitations of their current knowledge and experiences working with Two Spirit people as these insights are also absent in existing literature. This will foster future Indigenous-led community-based projects with an aim to improve Two Spirit peoples' health and wellness. Ten different sharing circles will be held with individuals residing in ten geographic locations across Canada including six in Saskatchewan and one each in Vancouver, Edmonton, Winnipeg, and Toronto. Informed by Indigenous methodologies, data will be recorded via notetaking and will be analyzed for themes. In addition to gaining knowledge and creating future collaborations between Two Spirit people and community pharmacies, this project aims to increase the visibility of and improve health outcomes for Two Spirit people in healthcare contexts. This research will produce opportunities for relationship building and knowledge sharing between the Two Spirit community and community pharmacists across Canada.

column36: Defining the involvement of the vasculature in survival and spread of brain tumour metastases
column37: Medulloblastoma (MB) is among the most common malignant pediatric brain tumours. Mortality among MB patients is mostly due to metastatic spread through the fluid surrounding the brain or through the bloodstream. Presently, there are no specific treatments targeting MB metastases. Preliminary data from the Taylor lab has found that metastatic tumour cells are closely associated with blood vessels-the tumour cells appear to be attached to the vessels. However, the specific anchors that contribute to tumour cell attachment on the blood vessels remain unclear. I hypothesize that the vasculatures act as a scaffold for the MB tumour cells and that the perivascular niche is important for metastatic cell colonization and survival. To investigate this, I will express a special niche labelling protein that glows, called sLP–mCherry, in patient-derived MB cells and then put them into mice. During tumour growth and metastasis, the sLP-mCherry protein from the MB cells will be released and taken up by the surrounding cells near the tumour. Later, I will look for the tumour microenvironment at the brain and spine. Because the protein glows I can use Fluorescent Activated Cell Sorting (FACS) to identify the vasculature associated cells (with sLP-mCherry) that were in close proximity to tumour cells. I will then perform single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on the FACS cells to identify the changes in the blood vessel gene expression in response to the tumour. This will allow us to identify the factors within the perivascular niche that may be supporting MB metastatic cell growth and survival, and then look for ways to stop the interaction and treat children with this devastating disease.

column36: Delivery of Factor Xa into transfusable platelets to increase their natural coagulability
column37: Platelets are blood cells that detect and adhere to sites of vascular damage, where they release pro-coagulant contents to initiate blood clotting. Failure to control bleeding after injury, such as during trauma, childbirth and surgery, accounts for more than half of all operating room deaths. Platelet transfusion is an essential treatment option to stop severe bleeding, but is not always effective, especially after significant blood loss. A strategy to improve platelet function during severe bleeds is to manipulate their internal composition by adding additional pro-coagulant proteins that enhance their natural ability to form a blood clot. This project aims to genetically engineer donor platelets to produce new coagulation factors so that after administration, they stop bleeding faster and create stronger clots than unmodified platelets. Generating new coagulation factors in platelets will be achieved by using lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug delivery technology. Similar LNPs that are being used in leading COVID-19 vaccine candidates developed by Moderna and BioNtech will be used to deliver nucleic acids into donor platelets. Internalization of specific nucleic acids by platelets will lead to the production of new pro-coagulant proteins, priming them for potent response to a bleeding event. Enhancing the natural coagulability of platelets will improve options for bleeding control after trauma, hopefully reducing the number of hemorrhage related deaths. Platelets have also been implicated in cancer and inflammatory diseases and enhancing coagulability using gene therapy will provide proof-of-concept that modified platelets can be used as a platform to deliver therapeutics in a multitude of disease contexts.

column36: Social Anxiety Disorder and Avoidant Personality Disorder: A Spectrum or Two Distinct Diagnoses?
column37: Social anxiety disorder (SAD) and avoidant personality disorder (AvPD) have long been considered two separate disorders, however the two disorders are remarkably similar in terms of characteristics. Individuals living with SAD fear the judgment of others which leads to distress and avoidance of social situations. Similarly, individuals living with AvPD are sensitive to scrutiny by others resulting in the avoidance of social situations. The shared characteristics of the two disorders has lead clinicians and researchers alike to question whether SAD and AvPD are in fact two distinct disorders or whether AvPD is simply a more severe version of SAD. In order to gain insight into this relationship, we are proposing a treatment outcome study where we will determine whether SAD and AvPD differ from one another based on comparing treatment outcomes. If SAD and AvPD differ only in terms of severity, as we hypothesize, then patients with SAD will experience greater symptom reduction and increased functioning in comparison to patients with AvPD. The results from this research will contribute to a greater understanding of the similarities and differences between SAD and AvPD. This knowledge will enable therapists to more effectively treat SAD and AvPD and thus, reduce the burden of these disorders on the mental health care system.

column36: Proteomic analyses of how ZIKV infection modulates the expression of astrocytic proteins involved in synaptogenesis and other synaptic controls
column37: Zika virus (ZIKV), one of the re-emerging viruses, is transmitted via a mosquito vector. It is an obligate micro-organism that requires host cells to replicate. To date, 87 countries show evidence of mosquito-borne ZIKV transmission. In Canada, 31,587 cases have been reported in 2018 with 3,473 of them having been confirmed via the lab results. Climate change potentially increases the incidence of mosquitoes impacting the viral transmission (Aedes aegyti prefers warm and rainy weather conditions). So far, no vaccine/treatment exists for ZIKV infection and its infection leads to numerous neurological conditions like microcephaly, abnormal brain development, Guillain-Barre syndrome, eye abnormalities, fetal growth impairment and fetal death. Inside the brain, specialized cells called astrocytes support neurons. Since these cells are one of the major brain cell populations and ZIKV is known to infect these cells, many of the above mentioned neurological diseases are associated with ZIKV impairing the astrocytic function and protein expression. According to my recently published data in 2019, ZIKV has been found to alter the expression of many such proteins like SPARC, STAT3, HSD17B10 and THBS 1/2, most of which are involved in the regulation of synapses. Therefore, this current project aims to focus on performing a proteomic screen looking at the impact of ZIKV infection in human astrocytic cells using mass spectrometry. Through this project, specific proteins inside ZIKV infected human astrocytes will be identified and their role in ZIKV replication, protein synthesis and assembly will be studied. This is crucial in understanding the mechanism of action of ZIKV as it will enable us to find novel therapeutic targets for various Zika antiviral treatments in the future.

column36: Psychoneuroendocrine study of stress reactivity and attachment in sexual and gender minority couples
column37: Social relationships can have significant beneficial effects on health. Research has shown that social support can alleviate stress, which in turn improves mental and overall health. The most important social relationships in adulthood are often romantic relationships. Indeed, the romantic partner is generally the first source of support a person turns to when experiencing stress. Although the association between partner support and stress is fairly well understood among heterosexual couples, very little is known about how it manifests itself in sexual and gender minority couples. Lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and queer (LGBTQ +) people experience particular stressors that have well-documented impacts on their stress response. In addition, evidence suggests that LGBTQ+ people may be more vulnerable to attachment difficulties (i.e. struggle in the way they relate to others and form close bonds). The objective of this study is to evaluate the buffering effect of partner support on the stress hormone cortisol response in heterosexual and LGBTQ+ couples. Participants will complete questionnaires relating to attachment, partner support, sexual orientation and gender identity. They will then be exposed to a stress paradigm (the Trier-Social Stress Test, TSST). Before, during, and after being exposed to the TSST, their stress response (i.e. their cortisol levels) will be recorded. Some participants will benefit from their partner's support when faced with the stressor, while others will face the stressor alone. This study will help better understand the relationship between sexual orientation, gender identity and stress reactivity. It will also help determine what role the attachment style of diverse couples plays on their stress response.

column36: Moral Injury and Canadian Health Care Workers During COVID-19: Experiences in a COVID-19 Unit
column37: Throughout the COVID-19 pandemic, health care workers (HCWs) have had to make difficult decisions in intense situations that put them at risk of developing moral injury (MI) (Greenberg et al., 2020). MI is a powerful psychological distress that emerges when one acts, or observes others act, in ways that violate their moral code (Nazarov et al., 2018). MI involves profound feelings of anger, guilt, shame and betrayal that can severely impair daily functioning (Jetly et al., 2020). Current recommendations on how to address COVID-19-related MI among HCWs lack the perspectives of HCWs themselves (e.g., Kok et al., 2020; Selman et al., 2020; Tracy et al., 2020; Williamson et al., 2020). The voices of HCWs are critical for preventing and treating MI. Without evidence-based interventions to support Canadian HCWs at this time, the Canadian health care system is at risk of a crisis because the labour of HCWs is critical to the health and well-being of all Canadians. In the proposed study, Canadian HCWs assigned to a COVID-19 unit will complete a 1-hour virtual interview about their experience with MI during COVID-19. Findings from this study will provide a comprehensive understanding of the morally injurious experiences that HCWs have endured during the pandemic. This research will direct evidence-based practices on how best to support Canadian HCWs at this time.

column36: The Role of the Chemokine Receptor CXCR3 Axis in the Efficacy of Oncolytic Vesicular Stomatitis Virus Therapy in Combination with Natural Killer T Cell Activation Immunotherapy in Melanoma
column37: One in forty-eight Canadians will develop melanoma in their lifetime, and the last two decades have seen a steady rise in melanoma cases. While surgery is highly effective in early melanoma, advanced melanoma is metastatic and resistant to traditional chemotherapies. Recently, novel cancer immunotherapies, such as oncolytic virus (OV) therapy, have made breakthroughs in advanced melanoma treatment, but their failure to induce complete responses in most patients points to a need for new and combined therapies. OVs, such as Vesicular Stomatitis Virus (VSV), selectively infect tumor cells with defective antiviral machinery. OVs are promising as they both directly kill tumor cells and indirectly increase immune activation within the tumor, leading to systemic immune responses targeting distant metastases. But OVs alone are unable to fully eliminate tumors. OV therapy has shown greater efficacy when combined with other immunotherapies such as Natural Killer T (NKT) cell activation therapy. My project will elucidate the indirect immune activating mechanisms of VSV, specifically its ability to upregulate chemokine CXCL9, -10, and -11 production in the tumor environment. These chemokines are crucial for orchestrating immune cell migration, differentiation, and activation, by binding to their receptor CXCR3 on target cells, which include T cells, Natural Killer (NK) cells, and NKT cells. By enhancing recruitment of these cells to the tumor, VSV enhances anti-tumor immune activation. I will investigate the importance of the CXCR3 axis for the efficacy of VSV and NKT cell activation immunotherapies, and establish an explanation for their synergistic combination. My project will hopefully prompt future studies maximizing combined immunotherapies, and inform clinical research.

column36: Exploring the contribution of transforming growth factor beta signalling to natural killer cell impairment in the pathogenesis of experimental pulmonary arterial hypertension
column37: Pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) is a deadly cardiovascular disease that affects thousands of men and women across Canada. PAH results from excessive growth of the cells lining the arteries in the lungs and causes restriction and blockage of blood flow from the right side of the heart. This puts the heart under immense stress, and often leads to death from right heart failure. Currently, treatments for PAH aim to lessen symptoms instead of targeting the true cause of the disease. Consequently, 15% of patients die each year. The natural killer (NK) cells of the immune system identify and remove stressed, infected or cancerous cells in the body. In addition to this role in immune surveillance, NK cells are involved in the formation of blood vessels needed for the development of the placenta during pregnancy. This function of NK cells is not limited to placental development and can also occur in other areas of the body, impacting vascular remodelling in diseases such as cancer and PAH. In these cases, it is thought that NK cells obtain this specialized function inappropriately after exposure to transforming growth factor beta (TGFB), a protein that is expressed in the uterus during pregnancy. Our lab has shown that NK cells are reduced in number and have impaired functions in PAH patients. We have also shown an increase in TGFB in these patients. However, the exact mechanism behind the disease-associated vascular remodelling is unknown. This project aims to clarify these mechanisms by using animal models to investigate the influence of TGFB on PAH development. We expect that animals lacking sensitivity to TGFB in their NK cells will be protected from developing disease. We hope that our findings will help find a better treatment for PAH patients.

column36: Blunted Neural Response to Reward as an Index of Stress Susceptibility and Depression in Women
column37: Major depressive disorder is one of the most common and costly diseases worldwide. Stress is a well-established risk factor for depression, but not all individuals who experience stress will develop depression. Understanding this relationship is now more critical than ever given that the world is experiencing a potent stressor-the COVID-19 pandemic-that is associated with rising levels of depressive symptoms, especially for women. One central need is to identify which individuals are at greatest risk for depression in the face of stress and to understand why. A blunted neural response to reward can be observed not only in people experiencing depression, but also in those at risk for the disorder suggesting that it may be a vulnerability marker for the illness. I believe stress may be key to explaining how these neural responses result in depression. In recent years, my lab has published many studies demonstrating that blunted neural responses to reward render individuals more vulnerable to the effects of stress. Specifically, the reward positivity (RewP), a fronto-central event-related potential (ERP) component that is sensitive to rewards and has been consistently linked to increased depressive symptoms and risk for depression. My proposed research will examine how baseline neural responses to reward predict who will be most likely to experience increases in depressive symptoms following pandemic-related stress. To test this question, I will leverage data from a sample of 109 pairs of women and their adolescent daughters who are vulnerable to depression. This study will be the first to examine reward-related ERPs as a moderator of the relationship between life stress and depression in women in the context of an acute stressor- the global COVID-19 pandemic.

column37: La 1re annee de baccalaureat coincide souvent au debut de la vie adulte. Les nouvelles responsabilites (p. ex., financieres) s'additionnent aux exigences academiques et contribuent a augmenter la vulnerabilite des etudiants aux problemes de sante mentale, surtout dans les programmes de sante. Des interventions sont disponibles pour limiter les consequences des problemes de sante mentale sur la carriere academique des etudiants en sante. Cependant, les evidences ne resument pas les interventions disponibles pour les etudiants en sante au baccalaureat et s'interessent plus frequemment a certains programmes d'etudes (p. ex., medecine). Les connaissances sur les interventions disponibles et sur l'efficacite et pertinence des interventions pour d'autres programmes de sante sont donc limitees. Les etudiants au baccalaureat en readaptation (ergotherapie, physiotherapie) sont parmi les programmes souvent oublies, toutefois, leurs besoins en sante mentale sont importants. Ce projet permettra de resumer les interventions disponibles pour les etudiants au baccalaureat en sante et d'explorer l'avis des etudiants de 1re annee en readaptation au sujet de leur pertinence. Un questionnaire en ligne sera transmis a l'ensemble des etudiants de 1re annee en ergotherapie et physiotherapie et 15 a 24 des etudiants de 1re annee seront invites a participer a des groupes de discussion. a partir de photos sur la vie etudiante, les groupes aborderont les interventions estimees pertinentes pour une vie etudiante saine. column36: A multimodal preoperative intervention combining exercise and nutrition for patients with lung cancer
column37: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) accounts for 80% of lung cancer patients in Canada. When diagnosed in early stages, patients are potential candidates for surgical tumour removal. However, these cancer patients often has a poor nutritional status and physical function as well as low muscle mass. These diminished health factors add to the major stress of surgery which negatively impacts recovery and survival. Patients may greatly benefit from nutrition supplementation and a structured exercise regime prior to surgery in hopes of optimizing functional status and stimulating muscle synthesis to improve their recovery afterwards, reduce complications and hospital length of stay. My research project will be embedded in a larger randomized controlled trial (RCT) for surgical patients with NSCLC where the main objective is to test the effect of a multimodal prehabilitation intervention which combines a mixed-nutrient supplement with structured exercise training or the supplement alone against a placebo, on functional pre- and post-operative outcomes. For the intervention groups, nutritional supplementation will include whey protein isolate matched to their body weight and needs (1.5 g/kg/d) which also contains a total of 6 g of leucine and 5 g of creatine. They will also ingest 15 mL of fish oil providing 2120 mg EPA, 1320 mg DHA and 1000 IU vitamin D3 per day. For those in the exercise and nutrition supplementation group, the structured physical activity will include aerobic and resistance training every second day. For my project, my objectives are to 1) relate changes in functional status to baseline nutritional status and 2) relate changes in muscle size and quality with nutritional and functional status during the 4-week pre-operative period in all three groups.
